1.183.s:
1.231
.. śeṣa uvāca .. ..
nṛṇāṃ grahagṛhītānāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ kathayāśu me ..
pratiṣedhaṃ ca dharmajña tatra me saṃśayo mahān .. .. 1 ..
1.183.d:
1.231
॥ शेष उवाच ॥ ॥
नृणां ग्रहगृहीतानां लक्षणं कथयाशु मे ॥
प्रतिषेधं च धर्मज्ञ तत्र मे संशयो महान् ॥ ॥ 1 ॥
1.183.m: Śeṣa said: / Declare quickly to me the signs of men seized by spirits / and the counter-measures, O knower of dharma; on that point I have great doubt.

1.183.s:
.. nāḍāyana uvāca .. ..
devarṣipitṛbhūtānāṃ satataṃ cāvamānanāt ..
guruvṛddhadvijācāryasiddhatāpasamardanāt .. 2 ..
1.183.d:
॥ नाडायन उवाच ॥ ॥
देवर्षिपितृभूतानां सततं चावमाननात् ॥
गुरुवृद्धद्विजाचार्यसिद्धतापसमर्दनात् ॥ 2 ॥
1.183.m: Nāḍāyana said: / From constantly disrespecting gods, sages, ancestors, and spirits, / from troubling teachers, elders, twice-born, preceptors, perfected ones, and ascetics,

1.183.s:
balimaṃgalahomādi niyamācāravarjanāt ..
vratādhyayanadharmādidhyānayogavyatikramāt .. 3 ..
1.183.d:
बलिमंगलहोमादि नियमाचारवर्जनात् ॥
व्रताध्ययनधर्मादिध्यानयोगव्यतिक्रमात् ॥ 3 ॥
1.183.m: from abandoning rules and conduct such as offerings, auspicious rites, and oblations, / from violating vows, study, dharma, meditation, and yoga,

1.183.s:
guḍāmiṣatilakṣaudramedhyairuccheṣitasya vā ..
śmaśānāyatanābhyāsaviṇmūtrotsarjanādapi .. 4 ..
1.183.d:
गुडामिषतिलक्षौद्रमेध्यैरुच्छेषितस्य वा ॥
श्मशानायतनाभ्यासविण्मूत्रोत्सर्जनादपि ॥ 4 ॥
1.183.m: or when one is smeared with leftovers of molasses, meat, sesame, honey, or pure foods, / and from discharging feces or urine near a cremation ground or temple,

1.183.s:
rātrau catuṣpathāraṇyaśūnyaveśmaniveśanāt ..
bhojanādbhinnabhāṇḍeṣu tathā maṃtracchalādapi .. 5 ..
1.183.d:
रात्रौ चतुष्पथारण्यशून्यवेश्मनिवेशनात् ॥
भोजनाद्भिन्नभाण्डेषु तथा मंत्रच्छलादपि ॥ 5 ॥
1.183.m: from entering at night a crossroads, forest, or empty dwelling, / from eating from broken vessels, and likewise through the deception of mantras,

1.183.s:
śmaśānacaityavṛkṣādi maithunādiniṣevaṇāt ..
avamānādabhīghātānmaṅgalānāmadarśanāt .. 6 ..
1.183.d:
श्मशानचैत्यवृक्षादि मैथुनादिनिषेवणात् ॥
अवमानादभीघातान्मङ्गलानामदर्शनात् ॥ 6 ॥
1.183.m: from engaging in sexual intercourse and the like in cremation grounds, at caitya trees, and such places, / from humiliation, physical trauma, and not witnessing auspicious things,

1.183.s:
īrṣyayā bandhuśāpācca rathyāvaskandhasevanāta ..
aiśvaryanāśācchokācca darpotsekātiharṣaṇāt .. 7 ..
1.183.d:
ईर्ष्यया बन्धुशापाच्च रथ्यावस्कन्धसेवनात ॥
ऐश्वर्यनाशाच्छोकाच्च दर्पोत्सेकातिहर्षणात् ॥ 7 ॥
1.183.m: out of envy, from a relative's curse, from resorting to the dust-heaps of public roads, / from the loss of sovereignty, from sorrow, from an excess of pride, from over-exhilaration,

1.183.s:
nirlajjanāstikānāṃ hi trāsitānāṃ viśeṣataḥ ..
gurubhiḥ samparityāgātkārttaghnyātsādhunindanāt .. 8 ..
1.183.d:
निर्लज्जनास्तिकानां हि त्रासितानां विशेषतः ॥
गुरुभिः सम्परित्यागात्कार्त्तघ्न्यात्साधुनिन्दनात् ॥ 8 ॥
1.183.m: especially of the shameless and unbelievers when terrified, / from abandonment by elders, from ingratitude, from censuring the virtuous,

1.183.s:
duḥkhātprajananātstrīṇāṃ mithyā caiva prabhāṣaṇāt ..
tuṣakeśakapālāsthikārpāsādiṣvadhiṣṭhitāt .. 9 ..
1.183.d:
दुःखात्प्रजननात्स्त्रीणां मिथ्या चैव प्रभाषणात् ॥
तुषकेशकपालास्थिकार्पासादिष्वधिष्ठितात् ॥ 9 ॥
1.183.m: from suffering, from women's childbirth, and from speaking falsehood, / from standing upon husks, hair, skulls, bones, cotton, and the like,

1.183.s:
prāṇināṃ sukhaduḥkheṣu tathā mṛtakasūtake ..
atyarthanaktasnāneṣu grahā gṛhṇanti mānavān .. 1.231.10 ..
1.183.d:
प्राणिनां सुखदुःखेषु तथा मृतकसूतके ॥
अत्यर्थनक्तस्नानेषु ग्रहा गृह्णन्ति मानवान् ॥ 1.231.10 ॥
1.183.m: in the pleasures and pains of living beings, and likewise at a death or birth impurity, / and during excessive bathing at night—spirits seize human beings.

1.183.s:
balaiśvaryavisaṃyogāddehamāviśati grahaḥ ..
jīvaḥ kukṣiṃ yathā dṛśyaḥ praviśanneva dṛśyate .. 11 ..
1.183.d:
बलैश्वर्यविसंयोगाद्देहमाविशति ग्रहः ॥
जीवः कुक्षिं यथा दृश्यः प्रविशन्नेव दृश्यते ॥ 11 ॥
1.183.m: A seizing spirit enters the body due to the disjunction of strength and sovereignty, / just as the soul [enters] the womb, not seen even as it enters.

1.183.s:
vanaspatīnvā ṛtavo vijñeyāśca tathā grahāḥ ..
kāraṇairnavabhidehaṃ graho gṛhṇāti dehinām ..12..
1.183.d:
वनस्पतीन्वा ऋतवो विज्ञेयाश्च तथा ग्रहाः ॥
कारणैर्नवभिदेहं ग्रहो गृह्णाति देहिनाम् ॥12॥
1.183.m: Or as seasons [enter] trees, so are seizing spirits to be understood; / for nine reasons does a seizing spirit seize the body of embodied beings:

1.183.s:
raudrasvabhāvāddhiṃsārthī ratyarthī balikāmukaḥ ..
vitrāsārthī balodrekādraudrātprāgdaihikādbhayāt .. 13 ..
1.183.d:
रौद्रस्वभावाद्धिंसार्थी रत्यर्थी बलिकामुकः ॥
वित्रासार्थी बलोद्रेकाद्रौद्रात्प्राग्दैहिकाद्भयात् ॥ 13 ॥
1.183.m: desiring violence from a terrible nature, desiring sexual pleasure, lusting for offerings, / desiring to terrify, from an excess of strength, from fierce terror belonging to a previous body,

1.183.s:
prayuktonyena mantraiśca graho gṛhṇāti mānavān ..
kāraṇāni tavoktāni yadyapyetāni pārthiva .. 14 ..
1.183.d:
प्रयुक्तोन्येन मन्त्रैश्च ग्रहो गृह्णाति मानवान् ॥
कारणानि तवोक्तानि यद्यप्येतानि पार्थिव ॥ 14 ॥
1.183.m: and directed by another through mantras, does a seizing spirit seize human beings. / Although these causes have been stated to you, O king,

1.183.s:
tathāpi traya evātra vijñeyāni vipaścitā ..
teṣāmantarbhavantyete yasmātpārthivasattama .. 15 ..
1.183.d:
तथापि त्रय एवात्र विज्ञेयानि विपश्चिता ॥
तेषामन्तर्भवन्त्येते यस्मात्पार्थिवसत्तम ॥ 15 ॥
1.183.m: nevertheless only three are to be recognized here by the wise, / because these [others] are included within them, O best of kings:

1.183.s:
balikāmastu ratyarthī hiṃsārthī ca tathā grahaḥ ..
asādhyaṃ balikāmaṃ tu kṛcchrasādhyaṃ ratigraham .. 16 ..
1.183.d:
बलिकामस्तु रत्यर्थी हिंसार्थी च तथा ग्रहः ॥
असाध्यं बलिकामं तु कृच्छ्रसाध्यं रतिग्रहम् ॥ 16 ॥
1.183.m: the spirit lusting for offerings, desiring sexual pleasure, and desiring violence. / The one lusting for offerings is incurable, but the spirit of sexual pleasure is curable with difficulty;

1.183.s:
hantukāmamasādhyantu vinā mantrabalaṃ mahat ..
sāṃtvapūrvaṃ graho viṣṭo madhuraṃ yaḥ prajāyate .. 17 ..
1.183.d:
हन्तुकाममसाध्यन्तु विना मन्त्रबलं महत् ॥
सांत्वपूर्वं ग्रहो विष्टो मधुरं यः प्रजायते ॥ 17 ॥
1.183.m: the one desiring to kill is incurable without great power of mantras. / When a spirit that has entered is preceded by gentleness and becomes sweet,

1.183.s:
tataścāntaramāsādya vicitraṃ yācate balim ..
pānamālyānulepāṃśca vaidyaṃ dṛṣṭvā namasyati .. 18 ..
1.183.d:
ततश्चान्तरमासाद्य विचित्रं याचते बलिम् ॥
पानमाल्यानुलेपांश्च वैद्यं दृष्ट्वा नमस्यति ॥ 18 ॥
1.183.m: and then, finding an opportunity, asks for manifold offerings, / drink, garlands, and ointments, and bows on seeing a physician—

1.183.s:
balikāmasya liṅgāni proktānyetāni vai mayā ..
ramate nṛtyati śucistathā hasati gāyati .. 19 ..
1.183.d:
बलिकामस्य लिङ्गानि प्रोक्तान्येतानि वै मया ॥
रमते नृत्यति शुचिस्तथा हसति गायति ॥ 19 ॥
1.183.m: these characteristics of one lusting for offerings have indeed been stated by me. / He plays, dances pure, laughs, and sings;

1.183.s:
gaṃdhamālyāmbarasnānadhūpodvarttanasevakaḥ ..
kathā vicitrāḥ kurute madhuraṃ samprabhāṣate .. 1.231.20 ..
1.183.d:
गंधमाल्याम्बरस्नानधूपोद्वर्त्तनसेवकः ॥
कथा विचित्राः कुरुते मधुरं सम्प्रभाषते ॥ 1.231.20 ॥
1.183.m: devoted to perfume, garlands, garments, bathing, incense, and unguents, / he tells wonderful stories and speaks sweetly;

1.183.s:
alaṃkṛtaṃ cāviśati varjayatyanalaṃkṛtam ..
ratikāmasya rūpāṇi jñeyānyetāni buddhinā .. 21 ..
1.183.d:
अलंकृतं चाविशति वर्जयत्यनलंकृतम् ॥
रतिकामस्य रूपाणि ज्ञेयान्येतानि बुद्धिना ॥ 21 ॥
1.183.m: he enters one who is adorned and avoids one unadorned: / these forms of one desiring sexual pleasure are to be known by the intelligent man.

1.183.s:
yaścāviṣṭo vidravati siṃhavyāghratarakṣupam ..
yuddhamārabhate karttuṃ gajādibhirabhītavat .. 22 ..
1.183.d:
यश्चाविष्टो विद्रवति सिंहव्याघ्रतरक्षुपम् ॥
युद्धमारभते कर्त्तुं गजादिभिरभीतवत् ॥ 22 ॥
1.183.m: And he who, when possessed, runs away, / or begins to fight lions, tigers, hyenas, and elephants fearlessly,

1.183.s:
bhṛśaṃ tāḍayati svāṅgaṃ patatyagnau pataṅgavat ..
rājadveṣāṇi kurute vijane ramate'dhikam .. 23 ..
1.183.d:
भृशं ताडयति स्वाङ्गं पतत्यग्नौ पतङ्गवत् ॥
राजद्वेषाणि कुरुते विजने रमतेऽधिकम् ॥ 23 ॥
1.183.m: beats his own limbs violently, falls into fire like a moth, / shows hostility to the king, and delights exceedingly in secluded places,

1.183.s:
karoti maraṇopāyānhantuṃ kāmārdito naraḥ ..
lomaharṣoṅgamāṃdyaṃ ca chāyāvaikṛtyameva ca .. 24 ..
1.183.d:
करोति मरणोपायान्हन्तुं कामार्दितो नरः ॥
लोमहर्षोङ्गमांद्यं च छायावैकृत्यमेव च ॥ 24 ॥
1.183.m: or the man, afflicted by desires, undertakes means of death to kill: / [there is] horripilation, sluggishness of limbs, and distortion of complexion,

1.183.s:
amānuṣotsāhabalaṃ vihārāhāraceṣṭitam ..
dvau vā trayo vā netre'sya saṃpaśyante kumārakāḥ .. 25 ..
1.183.d:
अमानुषोत्साहबलं विहाराहारचेष्टितम् ॥
द्वौ वा त्रयो वा नेत्रेऽस्य संपश्यन्ते कुमारकाः ॥ 25 ॥
1.183.m: superhuman energy and strength in his pastimes, food, and actions; / two or three pupils are seen in his eyes;

1.183.s:
nimīlitākṣitātyarthaṃ raktādivamanaṃ tathā ..
sāmānyametaduddiṣṭaṃ gṛhītasya tu lakṣaṇam .. 26 ..
1.183.d:
निमीलिताक्षितात्यर्थं रक्तादिवमनं तथा ॥
सामान्यमेतदुद्दिष्टं गृहीतस्य तु लक्षणम् ॥ 26 ॥
1.183.m: his eyes are excessively closed, and there is vomiting of blood and the like— / this has been stated as the general symptom of one who is seized.

1.183.s:
muktasya lakṣaṇaṃ cātaḥ pravakṣyāmi nibodhata ..
bhūmau vinipatatyāśu tathā saṃjñāṃ prapadyate .. 27 ..
1.183.d:
मुक्तस्य लक्षणं चातः प्रवक्ष्यामि निबोधत ॥
भूमौ विनिपतत्याशु तथा संज्ञां प्रपद्यते ॥ 27 ॥
1.183.m: And hereafter I shall declare the symptom of one released; listen: / he suddenly falls to the ground and then regains consciousness;

1.183.s:
parāmṛśati keśāṃśca vāsāṃsyābharaṇāni ca ..
śubhāśubhaṃ cātmakāryaṃ pṛcchati sma suhṛjjanam .. 28 ..
1.183.d:
परामृशति केशांश्च वासांस्याभरणानि च ॥
शुभाशुभं चात्मकार्यं पृच्छति स्म सुहृज्जनम् ॥ 28 ॥
1.183.m: he touches his hair, garments, and ornaments, / and inquires of his friends about his auspicious and inauspicious affairs.

1.183.s:
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi devādigrahalakṣaṇam ..
cikitsitena saṃyuktaṃ tannibodha janādhipa .. 29 ..
1.183.d:
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि देवादिग्रहलक्षणम् ॥
चिकित्सितेन संयुक्तं तन्निबोध जनाधिप ॥ 29 ॥
1.183.m: Hereafter I shall declare the characteristics of spirits of gods and others / along with their treatment; listen to that, O ruler of people.

1.183.s:
nadīkūlādriśikhararuciḥ prāsādameva ca ..
śuciśīla samācāro jñeyo devagrahārdditaḥ .. 1.231.30 ..
1.183.d:
नदीकूलाद्रिशिखररुचिः प्रासादमेव च ॥
शुचिशील समाचारो ज्ञेयो देवग्रहार्द्दितः ॥ 1.231.30 ॥
1.183.m: Fond of riverbanks, mountain peaks, and temples, / pure in character and conduct—he is to be known as afflicted by a divine spirit.

1.183.s:
devānāṃ pūjanaṃ tasya puṣpadhūpaphalākṣataiḥ ..
gandhadīpapradānaiśca vahnisantarpaṇaistathā .. 31 ..
1.183.d:
देवानां पूजनं तस्य पुष्पधूपफलाक्षतैः ॥
गन्धदीपप्रदानैश्च वह्निसन्तर्पणैस्तथा ॥ 31 ॥
1.183.m: Worship of the gods for him with flowers, incense, fruits, and unbroken grains, / with gifts of perfume and lamps, and likewise with offerings to the fire,

1.183.s:
gorasaiśca sa śālyannairbrāhmaṇaiḥ svastivācanaiḥ ..
karttavyaṃ viduṣā nityaṃ tataḥ saṃpadyate sukhī .. 32 ..
1.183.d:
गोरसैश्च स शाल्यन्नैर्ब्राह्मणैः स्वस्तिवाचनैः ॥
कर्त्तव्यं विदुषा नित्यं ततः संपद्यते सुखी ॥ 32 ॥
1.183.m: and with milk products, rice preparations, and benedictions recited by brahmins / should constantly be performed by the wise man; then he becomes happy.

1.183.s:
ucchiṣṭānbhairavānrāvānvirasaṃ kurute'dhikam ..
tasmiṃstathotsavānyakṣānvratānadhyayanāni ca .. 33 ..
1.183.d:
उच्छिष्टान्भैरवान्रावान्विरसं कुरुतेऽधिकम् ॥
तस्मिंस्तथोत्सवान्यक्षान्व्रतानध्ययनानि च ॥ 33 ॥
1.183.m: He emits impure, terrible roars, excessively harsh; / he [despises] festivals, yakṣas, vows, and recitations of sacred texts;

1.183.s:
bahuśo vaṭucāśnāti vastraṃ pāṭayati svakam ..
asuragrahaduṣṭasya rūpametadvinirddiśet .. 34 ..
1.183.d:
बहुशो वटुचाश्नाति वस्त्रं पाटयति स्वकम् ॥
असुरग्रहदुष्टस्य रूपमेतद्विनिर्द्दिशेत् ॥ 34 ॥
1.183.m: he eats frequently and voraciously, and tears his own garment— / one should declare this to be the appearance of one afflicted by an asura spirit.

1.183.s:
daityasaṃpūjanaṃ tasya kāryaṃ māṃsasurāsavaiḥ ..
raktaiḥ puṣpairdhūpadīpaistathā bījasamudbhavaiḥ .. 35 ..
1.183.d:
दैत्यसंपूजनं तस्य कार्यं मांससुरासवैः ॥
रक्तैः पुष्पैर्धूपदीपैस्तथा बीजसमुद्भवैः ॥ 35 ॥
1.183.m: Worship of the daityas must be performed for him with meat, wine, and liquor, / with red flowers, incense, lamps, and things produced from seeds.

1.183.s:
gandharvavādyanirghoṣaṃ śrutvā hṛṣṭaḥ pranṛtyati ..
tīrthodyānanadītīragandhamālyādisevanāt .. 36 ..
1.183.d:
गन्धर्ववाद्यनिर्घोषं श्रुत्वा हृष्टः प्रनृत्यति ॥
तीर्थोद्याननदीतीरगन्धमाल्यादिसेवनात् ॥ 36 ॥
1.183.m: Hearing the sound of gandharva musical instruments, he rejoices and dances; / from frequenting sacred bathing places, gardens, riverbanks, perfumes, and garlands,

1.183.s:
yathākāmaṃ vicarati gandharvonmādito naraḥ ..
gandhairmālyaiśca vividhairgītavādyaistathaiva ca .. 37 ..
1.183.d:
यथाकामं विचरति गन्धर्वोन्मादितो नरः ॥
गन्धैर्माल्यैश्च विविधैर्गीतवाद्यैस्तथैव च ॥ 37 ॥
1.183.m: the man maddened by a gandharva roams about at will. / With various perfumes and garlands, and likewise with songs and musical instruments,

1.183.s:
gandharvapūjanaṃ kāryaṃ tena saṃpadyate sukhī ..
nidrāluralaso duṣṭo darvīvatkurute karau .. 38 ..
1.183.d:
गन्धर्वपूजनं कार्यं तेन संपद्यते सुखी ॥
निद्रालुरलसो दुष्टो दर्वीवत्कुरुते करौ ॥ 38 ॥
1.183.m: worship of the gandharvas must be performed; thereby he becomes happy. / Sleepy, sluggish, corrupt, he makes his hands like a snake's hood;

1.183.s:
garbhavāsaguhāsevī naronmattaṃ vidurbudhāḥ ..
nāgānāṃ pūjanaṃ tasya kāryaṃ kulmāṣaparpaṭaiḥ .. 39 ..
1.183.d:
गर्भवासगुहासेवी नरोन्मत्तं विदुर्बुधाः ॥
नागानां पूजनं तस्य कार्यं कुल्माषपर्पटैः ॥ 39 ॥
1.183.m: resorting to the inner chambers and caves, the wise know the man to be mad. / Worship of the nāgas must be performed for him with boiled sour pulses and crisps,

1.183.s:
pāyasollopikāpūpaiḥ padmotpalabisaistathā ..
amatsarī mṛdurvīraḥ priyavāgbahubhojanaḥ .. 1.231.40 ..
1.183.d:
पायसोल्लोपिकापूपैः पद्मोत्पलबिसैस्तथा ॥
अमत्सरी मृदुर्वीरः प्रियवाग्बहुभोजनः ॥ 1.231.40 ॥
1.183.m: with rice boiled in milk, sweetmeats, cakes, and lotus roots. / Free from envy, gentle, valiant, speaking pleasant words, eating much,

1.183.s:
pṛthuvihvalatāmrākṣaḥ tathā vai gorasapriyaḥ ..
bhūtonmādasamāviṣṭo liṅgairetairvinirdiśet .. 41 ..
1.183.d:
पृथुविह्वलताम्राक्षः तथा वै गोरसप्रियः ॥
भूतोन्मादसमाविष्टो लिङ्गैरेतैर्विनिर्दिशेत् ॥ 41 ॥
1.183.m: with broad, rolling, copper-colored eyes, and fond indeed of milk products— / one should designate one possessed by spirit-madness by these signs.

1.183.s:
kusumairbahuvarṇaiśca gorasairvividhaistathā ..
bhūtapūjā tu karttavyā tena sampadyate sukhī .. 42 ..
1.183.d:
कुसुमैर्बहुवर्णैश्च गोरसैर्विविधैस्तथा ॥
भूतपूजा तु कर्त्तव्या तेन सम्पद्यते सुखी ॥ 42 ॥
1.183.m: With many-colored blossoms and likewise with various milk products, / worship of the spirits must be performed; thereby he becomes happy.

1.183.s:
śūnyāgāraśmaśānādricatuṣpathaniṣevakaḥ ..
rātrau carati yocchiṣṭaḥ piśāconmādito naraḥ .. 43 ..
1.183.d:
शून्यागारश्मशानाद्रिचतुष्पथनिषेवकः ॥
रात्रौ चरति योच्छिष्टः पिशाचोन्मादितो नरः ॥ 43 ॥
1.183.m: Frequenting empty houses, cremation grounds, mountains, and crossroads, / a man driven mad by a piśāca roams about at night while polluted by leftover food.

1.183.s:
piśācayajanaṃ tasya karttavyaṃ palalāmiṣaiḥ ..
kaṇṭakīsambhavaiḥ puṣpaiḥ kṛṣṇavarṇaistathaiva ca .. 44 ..
1.183.d:
पिशाचयजनं तस्य कर्त्तव्यं पललामिषैः ॥
कण्टकीसम्भवैः पुष्पैः कृष्णवर्णैस्तथैव च ॥ 44 ॥
1.183.m: A sacrifice to the piśācas must be performed for him with ground sesame, flesh, / flowers from thorny plants, and black-colored [offerings].

1.183.s:
avyaktabhāṣī raktākṣo hāsye coccasvarastathā ..
raudraṃ nirīkṣate'tyarthaṃ yakṣenonmādito naraḥ ..45..
1.183.d:
अव्यक्तभाषी रक्ताक्षो हास्ये चोच्चस्वरस्तथा ॥
रौद्रं निरीक्षतेऽत्यर्थं यक्षेनोन्मादितो नरः ॥45॥
1.183.m: Speaking incoherently, red-eyed, laughing with a loud voice, / a man driven mad by a yakṣa glares terribly.

1.183.s:
kulmāṣaghṛtapiṇyākapalalollopikāguḍaiḥ ..
yakṣāṇāṃ pūjanaṃ tasya kartavyaṃ doṣaśāntaye .. 46 ..
1.183.d:
कुल्माषघृतपिण्याकपललोल्लोपिकागुडैः ॥
यक्षाणां पूजनं तस्य कर्तव्यं दोषशान्तये ॥ 46 ॥
1.183.m: Worship of the yakṣas must be performed for him with sour gruel, clarified butter, oil-cake, ground sesame, cakes, and molasses, / for the pacification of the affliction.

1.183.s:
udvignacetāḥ śītaśca nātiśokaparāyaṇaḥ ..
rākṣasena gṛhītaśca bhavatyoṣṭhavilehakaḥ .. 47 ..
1.183.d:
उद्विग्नचेताः शीतश्च नातिशोकपरायणः ॥
राक्षसेन गृहीतश्च भवत्योष्ठविलेहकः ॥ 47 ॥
1.183.m: His mind agitated, feeling cold, not excessively prone to grief, / he who is seized by a rākṣasa constantly licks his lips.

1.183.s:
pakvāmiṣeṇa māṃsena rudhireṇa tathaiva ca ..
rākṣasānāṃ baliḥ kāryastasya doṣapraśāntaye .. 48 ..
1.183.d:
पक्वामिषेण मांसेन रुधिरेण तथैव च ॥
राक्षसानां बलिः कार्यस्तस्य दोषप्रशान्तये ॥ 48 ॥
1.183.m: An oblation must be made to the rākṣasas with cooked meat, raw flesh, / and blood, for the pacification of his affliction.

1.183.s:
bhasmapāṃśurajodhvasto malino malināmbaraḥ ..
pretagṛhīto bhavati vikṛto dhvastamastakaḥ .. 49 ..
1.183.d:
भस्मपांशुरजोध्वस्तो मलिनो मलिनाम्बरः ॥
प्रेतगृहीतो भवति विकृतो ध्वस्तमस्तकः ॥ 49 ॥
1.183.m: Covered in ash, dust, and grime, filthy, wearing dirty clothes, / he who is seized by a deceased spirit is deformed, with his head covered [in dust].

1.183.s: odanaṃ madhupānīyaṃ sarpiḥ kṣīrasamanvitam .. 1.231.50 ..
1.183.d: ओदनं मधुपानीयं सर्पिः क्षीरसमन्वितम् ॥ 1.231.50 ॥
1.183.m: Boiled rice, honey-water, clarified butter mixed with milk,

1.183.s:
pretānāṃ tatra dātavyaṃ tena saṃpadyate sukhī ..
śuciḥ śucisamācāraḥ sandhyācārī tilapriyaḥ .. 51 ..
1.183.d:
प्रेतानां तत्र दातव्यं तेन संपद्यते सुखी ॥
शुचिः शुचिसमाचारः सन्ध्याचारी तिलप्रियः ॥ 51 ॥
1.183.m: must be given there to the deceased spirits; thereby he becomes happy. / Pure, pure in conduct, moving about at twilight, fond of sesame,

1.183.s:
pitṛgrahagṛhītasya rūpametadvinirdiśeta ..
tilagorasapuṣpānnamadhumūlaphalaiḥ śubhaiḥ .. 52 ..
1.183.d:
पितृग्रहगृहीतस्य रूपमेतद्विनिर्दिशेत ॥
तिलगोरसपुष्पान्नमधुमूलफलैः शुभैः ॥ 52 ॥
1.183.m: this is declared to be the appearance of one seized by the seizure of the ancestors. / With sesame, dairy products, flowers, food, honey, roots, and auspicious fruits,

1.183.s:
dīpairdānaistathā nityaṃ praṇipātena cājñayā ..
pitṝṇāṃ pūjanaṃ tasya karttavyaṃ doṣaśāntaye .. 53 ..
1.183.d:
दीपैर्दानैस्तथा नित्यं प्रणिपातेन चाज्ञया ॥
पितॄणां पूजनं तस्य कर्त्तव्यं दोषशान्तये ॥ 53 ॥
1.183.m: with lamps, gifts constantly, prostration, and obedience, / worship of the ancestors must be performed for him to pacify the affliction.

1.183.s:
adhīte japate caiva śucistiṣṭhati cāpyatha ..
yogāsaktastathārṣeṇa gṛhīto mānavo bhavet .. 54 ..
1.183.d:
अधीते जपते चैव शुचिस्तिष्ठति चाप्यथ ॥
योगासक्तस्तथार्षेण गृहीतो मानवो भवेत् ॥ 54 ॥
1.183.m: Reciting, muttering prayers, remaining pure, / and attached to yoga—a man seized by a seer [spirit] becomes such.

1.183.s:
havirgorasapuṣpādyaistathā'dhyayanasaṃstavaiḥ ..
ṛṣīṇāṃ pūjanaṃ kāryaṃ tasya doṣapraśānnaye .. 55 ..
1.183.d:
हविर्गोरसपुष्पाद्यैस्तथाऽध्ययनसंस्तवैः ॥
ऋषीणां पूजनं कार्यं तस्य दोषप्रशान्नये ॥ 55 ॥
1.183.m: Worship of the seers must be performed for him with sacrificial offerings, dairy products, flowers and the like, / as well as recitation and eulogies, for the pacification of his affliction.

1.183.s:
karmaprasakto bhavati na nidrāṃ bhajate divā ..
pauruṣeṇa gṛhītasya lakṣaṇaṃ samudāhṛtama .. 56 ..
1.183.d:
कर्मप्रसक्तो भवति न निद्रां भजते दिवा ॥
पौरुषेण गृहीतस्य लक्षणं समुदाहृतम ॥ 56 ॥
1.183.m: Constantly attached to activity, he does not take sleep by day— / this is declared to be the characteristic of one seized by a human [spirit].

1.183.s:
brāhmaṇānbhojayettatra miṣṭamannaṃ susaṃskṛtam ..
gandhamālyojvalānrājaṃstasya doṣapraśāntaye .. 57 ..
1.183.d:
ब्राह्मणान्भोजयेत्तत्र मिष्टमन्नं सुसंस्कृतम् ॥
गन्धमाल्योज्वलान्राजंस्तस्य दोषप्रशान्तये ॥ 57 ॥
1.183.m: One should feed brahmins there with sweet, well-prepared food, / radiant with perfumes and garlands, O king, for the pacification of his affliction.

1.183.s:
skandagrahagṛhītānāṃ bālānāṃ śṛṇu lakṣaṇama ..
roditi stanati dhyāti bhūmau svapiti cāsakṛt .. 58 ..
1.183.d:
स्कन्दग्रहगृहीतानां बालानां शृणु लक्षणम ॥
रोदिति स्तनति ध्याति भूमौ स्वपिति चासकृत् ॥ 58 ॥
1.183.m: Hear the symptom of children seized by the seizure of Skanda: / he weeps, groans, broods, and sleeps repeatedly on the ground,

1.183.s:
asambaddhapralāpī vā jñeyaḥ skandagrahārdditaḥ ..
raktaiḥ puṣpaiḥ phalairmūlaiḥ bālakrīḍanakaistathā .. 59 ..
1.183.d:
असम्बद्धप्रलापी वा ज्ञेयः स्कन्दग्रहार्द्दितः ॥
रक्तैः पुष्पैः फलैर्मूलैः बालक्रीडनकैस्तथा ॥ 59 ॥
1.183.m: or prattles incoherently—he is to be known as afflicted by the seizure of Skanda. / With red flowers, fruits, roots, and children’s toys,

1.183.s:
ghaṇṭā ca kukkuṭaiḥ pūjā balinā vividhena ca ..
patākābhiśca karttavyā kumārasya mahātmanaḥ .. 1.231.60 ..
1.183.d:
घण्टा च कुक्कुटैः पूजा बलिना विविधेन च ॥
पताकाभिश्च कर्त्तव्या कुमारस्य महात्मनः ॥ 1.231.60 ॥
1.183.m: and a bell, cocks, worship with diverse oblations, / and banners, [the rite] should be performed for the great-souled Kumāra.

1.183.s:
ataḥ paraṃ lokahitaṃ tavādya sarvagrahaghnānnipuṇānprayogān ..
vakṣyāmi yeṣāṃ hi niṣevaṇena grahairvimucyanti narā narendrān .. 61 ..
1.232
.. nāḍāyana uvāca ..
abhyaṅgotsādanaṃ snānaṃ dhūpo rakṣābalirghṛtama ..
netrāñjanaṃ pradhavanaṃ navagrahaharāḥ kriyāḥ .. 1 ..
sarpagandhā vacā kuṣṭhamustākṣepaṇacandanaiḥ ..
sakṣīramūtrairvipacettailaṃ sarvagrahāpaham .. 2 ..
bilvamadhyaṃ brahmadatta gavākṣībṛhatīphalam ..
utsādanamidaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ ślakṣṇapiṣṭaṃ jalena tu .. 3 ..
uśīrakuṣṭhamañjiṣṭhādevadārumanaḥśilāḥ ..
śrīveṣṭakastathā kauntī haritālailavāluke .. 4 ..
etaccūrṇīkṛtaṃ sarvaṃ pañcagavyāṃśamiśritam ..
sarvagrahapraśamanaṃ snānamāyuṣyamuttamam ..5..
sarṣapāśca khuraṃ kuṣṭaṃ ghṛtaṃ bhallātakaṃ vacā..
pūtīkamajamodā ca dhūpaḥ sarvagrahāpahaḥ ..6..
1.183.d:
अतः परं लोकहितं तवाद्य सर्वग्रहघ्नान्निपुणान्प्रयोगान् ॥
वक्ष्यामि येषां हि निषेवणेन ग्रहैर्विमुच्यन्ति नरा नरेन्द्रान् ॥ 61 ॥
1.232
॥ नाडायन उवाच ॥
अभ्यङ्गोत्सादनं स्नानं धूपो रक्षाबलिर्घृतम ॥
नेत्राञ्जनं प्रधवनं नवग्रहहराः क्रियाः ॥ 1 ॥
सर्पगन्धा वचा कुष्ठमुस्ताक्षेपणचन्दनैः ॥
सक्षीरमूत्रैर्विपचेत्तैलं सर्वग्रहापहम् ॥ 2 ॥
बिल्वमध्यं ब्रह्मदत्त गवाक्षीबृहतीफलम् ॥
उत्सादनमिदं श्रेष्ठं श्लक्ष्णपिष्टं जलेन तु ॥ 3 ॥
उशीरकुष्ठमञ्जिष्ठादेवदारुमनःशिलाः ॥
श्रीवेष्टकस्तथा कौन्ती हरितालैलवालुके ॥ 4 ॥
एतच्चूर्णीकृतं सर्वं पञ्चगव्यांशमिश्रितम् ॥
सर्वग्रहप्रशमनं स्नानमायुष्यमुत्तमम् ॥5॥
सर्षपाश्च खुरं कुष्टं घृतं भल्लातकं वचा॥
पूतीकमजमोदा च धूपः सर्वग्रहापहः ॥6॥
1.183.m:
Hereafter, for the welfare of the world, I shall tell you today skillful remedies destroying all seizures, / through the application of which men are freed from seizures, O best of kings.
1.232 / Nāḍāyana said: / Anointing, rubbing with paste, bathing, incense, protective oblation, clarified butter, / collyrium for the eyes, and fumigation are the rites that remove the nine seizures.
With sarpagandhā, sweet flag, costus, nut grass, akṣepaṇa, and sandalwood, / one should boil oil with milk and urine; it removes all seizures.
Bael pulp, brahmadatta, colocynth, and nightshade fruit— / this is an excellent paste for rubbing when finely ground with water.
Khus grass, costus, Indian madder, deodar cedar, realgar, / turpentine resin, kauntī, orpiment, and elavāluka—
all this powdered and mixed with a portion of the five products of the cow / is an excellent bath that pacifies all seizures and promotes longevity.
Mustard seeds, hoof, costus, clarified butter, marking nut, sweet flag, / pūtīka, and bishop's weed are an incense that removes all seizures.

1.183.s:
śastraṃ vā rocanaṃ śastaṃ suvarṇaṃ maṇimauktikam ..
viṣaṃ savatsāṃ dhenuṃ ca mattaṃ chāgaṃ tathaiva ca .. 7 ..
pūrṇakumbhaṃ ca maṃtrāśca vīṇā candanameva ca ..
mayūrapakṣānrajataṃ samārgaṇaguṇaṃ dhanuḥ .. 8 ..
bhallātakāni sarpiśca rakṣārthaṃ dhārayedgṛhe ..
puṣpairdhūpaistathā gandhairbhakṣyairnānāvidhaistathā .. 9 ..
pūrṇakumbhaiḥ sakulmāṣairgorasaiścandanena ca ..
dhūpairannaprakāraiśca baliḥ kāryo vijānatā .. 1.232.10 ..
kāyasthāṃ ja ṭilāṃ vīrāṃ vayasthāṃ nakulīdvayam ..
jayāṃ ca vijayāṃ caiva mānāṃ parpaṭakambarīm .. 11 ..
markaṭīṃ sūkarīṃ chatrāmaticchatrāṃ palaṅkaṣām ..
rāmāṃ pūtanakāṃ keśīṃ māraṭāṃ kaṭukāṃ vacām ..12..
caurakāṃ viṣṇudattāṃ ca vṛṣṭikāṇḍīṃ ca cūrṇayet ..
purāṇamebhirvipacedghṛtaṃ toye caturguṇe .. 13 ..
1.183.d:
शस्त्रं वा रोचनं शस्तं सुवर्णं मणिमौक्तिकम् ॥
विषं सवत्सां धेनुं च मत्तं छागं तथैव च ॥ 7 ॥
पूर्णकुम्भं च मंत्राश्च वीणा चन्दनमेव च ॥
मयूरपक्षान्रजतं समार्गणगुणं धनुः ॥ 8 ॥
भल्लातकानि सर्पिश्च रक्षार्थं धारयेद्गृहे ॥
पुष्पैर्धूपैस्तथा गन्धैर्भक्ष्यैर्नानाविधैस्तथा ॥ 9 ॥
पूर्णकुम्भैः सकुल्माषैर्गोरसैश्चन्दनेन च ॥
धूपैरन्नप्रकारैश्च बलिः कार्यो विजानता ॥ 1.232.10 ॥
कायस्थां ज टिलां वीरां वयस्थां नकुलीद्वयम् ॥
जयां च विजयां चैव मानां पर्पटकम्बरीम् ॥ 11 ॥
मर्कटीं सूकरीं छत्रामतिच्छत्रां पलङ्कषाम् ॥
रामां पूतनकां केशीं मारटां कटुकां वचाम् ॥12॥
चौरकां विष्णुदत्तां च वृष्टिकाण्डीं च चूर्णयेत् ॥
पुराणमेभिर्विपचेद्घृतं तोये चतुर्गुणे ॥ 13 ॥
1.183.m:
A weapon or ox-gall is recommended, gold, a gem, a pearl, / poison, a cow with her calf, and an intoxicated he-goat;
a filled jar, mantras, a vīṇā, and sandalwood, / peacock feathers, silver, and a bow strung with an arrow;
one should keep marking nuts and clarified butter in the house for protection. / With flowers, incense, perfumes, and diverse kinds of edible foods,
with filled jars, with sour gruel, dairy products, sandalwood, / incenses, and varieties of food, the wise man should offer an oblation.
Kāyasthā, jaṭilā, vīrā, vayasthā, both kinds of nakulī, / jayā, vijayā, mānā, and parpaṭakambarī,
markaṭī, sūkarī, chatrā, aticchatrā, palaṅkaṣā, / rāmā, pūtanakā, keśī, māraṭā, kaṭukā, sweet flag,
caurakā, viṣṇudattā, and vṛṣṭikāṇḍī one should powder; / with these, one should boil aged clarified butter in four times the amount of water.

1.183.d:
महापैशाचकं नाम सर्वग्रहनिवारणम् ॥
रसाञ्जनं त्रिकटुकं मञ्जिष्ठा समनःशिला ॥ 14 ॥
समानि च्छागमूत्रेण पिष्ट्वा वर्तिन्तु कारयेत् ॥
छाया शुष्कं तु तं कुर्यादञ्जनं ग्रहनाशनम् ॥ 15 ॥
श्वेतज्योतिष्मतीं व्योषं वस्त्रसूत्रेण वेष्टितम् ॥
छायाशुष्के पुनः पिष्टं ज्ञेयं प्रशमनं हितम् ॥ ॥ 16 ॥
संपूजनं देवगुरुद्विजानां भक्तिः परा चक्रगदाधरस्य ॥
येषां न तेषां प्रभवन्ति दीपा ग्रहोद्भवा भूमिपतिप्रधान ॥ 17 ॥
1.233
॥ शैलूष उवाच ॥ ॥
स्कन्दस्य शरणं प्राप्तान्ग्रहाञ्श्रुत्वा शतक्रतुः ॥
यश्चकार महाभाग तन्ममाचक्ष्व पृच्छतः ॥ 1 ॥
॥ नाडायन उवाच ॥
स्कन्दस्य शरणं प्राप्ताञ्श्रुत्वा शतमखो ययौ ॥
देवदेवगणैः सार्द्धं स्कन्दो यत्र व्यवस्थितः ॥ 2 ॥
1.183.m:
It is named Mahāpaiśācaka, warding off all seizures. / Extract of Indian barberry, the three pungents, Indian madder, and realgar—
having ground equal parts with goat's urine, one should fashion a wick; / drying it in the shade, one should prepare that collyrium which destroys seizures.
White jyotiṣmatī and the three pungents wrapped in a cloth thread / and dried in the shade, then ground again, should be known as a wholesome pacifier.
For those who have the worship of the gods, guru, and twice-born, and supreme devotion to the Wielder of the Discus and Mace, / the blazing fires arising from seizures do not prevail, O foremost of kings.
1.233 / Śailūṣa said: / Having heard of the seizures that took refuge with Skanda, what Śatakratu / did, O illustrious one, tell that to me who am asking.
Nāḍāyana said: / Having heard of those who had taken refuge with Skanda, Śatamakhu went / together with the hosts of gods to where Skanda was stationed.

skandaṃ deveśvaro dṛṣṭvā dīptatejaḥsamadyutim ..

1.183.d:
स्कन्दं देवेश्वरो दृष्ट्वा दीप्ततेजःसमद्युतिम् ॥
तुष्टाव राजशार्दूल प्रयतः सुसमाहितः ॥ 3 ॥
॥ शक्र उवाच ॥ ॥
देवदेवं नमस्यामि कुमारं वरमच्युतम् ॥
कार्तिकेयं दुराराध्यं वह्नितेजः समुद्भवम् ॥ 4 ॥
उमाशङ्करजं भीमं गङ्गया जठरे धृतम् ॥
शक्तिहस्तं विशालाक्षं षण्मुखं दीप्ततेजसम् ॥ 5 ॥
भक्तानुकम्पिनं दांतं ब्रह्मण्यं वरदं प्रभुम् ॥
काकपक्षधरं शांतं शिखण्डकविभूषितम् ॥ 6 ॥
रक्ताम्बरं महाबाहुं मयूरवरगामिनम् ॥
घण्टाप्रियं गणाध्यक्षं महाबलपराक्रमम् ॥ ॥ 7 ॥
देवसेनापतिं देवं सर्वलोकहितेप्सया ॥
षष्ठ्यान्तु शुक्लपक्षस्य ये च त्वां भौमवासरे ॥8॥
कृत्तिकास्वर्चयिष्यन्ति यथालाभं पृथक्पृथक् ॥
न तेषां दुर्ल्लभं किञ्चिद्भविष्यति सुरोत्तम ॥ 9 ॥
1.183.m:
Having seen Skanda, whose brilliance was equal to blazing fire, / the lord of the gods praised him, O tiger among kings, disciplined and well-composed.
Śakra said: / I bow to the god of gods, Kumāra, the excellent, unfallen one, / Kārtikeya, difficult to appease, born of the fire's brilliance.
[I bow to him] born of Umā and Śaṅkara, fierce, borne in the womb by Gaṅgā, / holding a spear in his hand, large-eyed, six-faced, and of blazing splendour,
compassionate to his devotees, subdued, devoted to brahmins, grantor of boons, the lord, / wearing side-locks of hair, tranquil, adorned with crest-feathers,
wearing red garments, mighty-armed, riding upon an excellent peacock, / fond of bells, leader of the troops, of great strength and valor,
the god who is the commander of the army of the gods, desiring the welfare of all the worlds. / And those who, on the sixth lunar day of the bright fortnight, on a Tuesday,
worship you during [the asterism of] the Kṛttikās individually according to their means, / nothing will be difficult for them to obtain, O foremost of the gods.

1.183.d:
द्वियोगे द्विगुणं तेषां फलं स्कन्द भविष्यति ॥
त्रियोगे पूजनं कृत्वा भवतः सुरसत्तम ॥ 1.233.10 ॥
अक्षयं फलमाप्स्यन्ति नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
वैशाखमासादारभ्य पञ्चम्यां य उपोषितः ॥ 11 ॥
भवन्तं पूजयेत्षष्ठ्यां संवत्सरमतन्द्रितः ॥
पुत्रार्थी लभते पुत्रान्धनकामो धनानि च ॥ 12 ॥
मृतश्च प्राप्नुयात्स्वर्गं त्वयि तुष्टे हरात्मज ॥
स्तोत्रेण च मदीयेन ये स्तोष्यन्ति तव प्रभो ॥ ॥ 13 ॥
लोकद्वयेऽपि ते कामान्प्राप्स्यन्ति मनसेप्सितान् ॥
॥ स्कन्द उवाच ॥ ॥
पिता मे दैवतं शक्र महादेवः प्रतापवान् ॥ 14 ॥
तस्याज्ञया करिष्यामि यन्मां वक्ष्यति वासव ॥
॥ नाडायन उवाच ॥ ॥
ततः प्रादुरभूत्तत्र देवदेवस्त्रिलोचनः ॥ 15 ॥
अभ्यषिञ्चत्कुमारं च ब्रह्मणा सहितः प्रभुः ॥
सेनापत्येन देवानां सोऽभिषिक्तस्तदा प्रभो ॥ 16 ॥
1.183.m:
In a conjunction of two [of these], their reward will be doubled, O Skanda; / and having performed worship of you in a conjunction of three, O best of the gods,
they will attain an imperishable fruit; there should be no doubt in this matter. / Beginning from the month of Vaiśākha, he who, fasting on the fifth,
worships you on the sixth for a full year without slackening— / one desiring sons obtains sons, and one desiring wealth [obtains] riches.
And upon dying, he will attain heaven when you are pleased, O son of Hara. / And those who will praise you with my hymn of praise, O lord,
will obtain the desires longed for in their minds in both worlds. / Skanda said: / My father, O Śakra, is the god Mahādeva, full of majesty.
By his command I shall do whatever he tells me, O Vāsava. / Nāḍāyana said: / Then the god of gods, the three-eyed one, appeared there.
Together with Brahmā, the lord consecrated Kumāra. / Then consecrated into the generalship of the gods, O lord,

1.183.d:
जघान महिषं नाम दानवं देवकण्टकम् ॥
महिषेन समान्वीर्ये जघानायुतशोऽपरान् ॥ 17 ॥
बहुत्वाद्दानवान्वीरः स्कन्दः परबलार्द्दनः ॥
यदा हन्तुं न शक्नोति तदा देवस्त्रिलोचनः ॥ 18 ॥
जघान मनसा तत्र ततः शूलवरायुधः ॥
जघान दानवानन्याञ्शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः ॥ 19 ॥
भक्ताऽनुकम्पी भगवांस्त्रिनेत्रो देवारिसंघान्विनिपात्य संघे ॥
कृत्वा त्रिलोकीं च तदा प्रहृष्टां जगाम कैलासगिरिं महात्मा ॥ 1.233.20 ॥ ॥
1.234
॥ नाडायन उवाच ॥ ॥
तस्यैव देवदवस्य प्रभावमपरं शृणु ॥
यष्टुकामैः सुरैः पूर्वं यज्ञे भागो न कल्पितः ॥ 1 ॥
यदा राजंस्त्रिनेत्रस्य तदा क्रुद्धेन शंभुना ॥
यज्ञवाटं ततो गत्वा देवा वित्रासिता बलात् ॥ 2 ॥
पुरोडाशं भक्षयित्वा पूष्णो दन्तानशातयत ॥
भगस्य नयनं वामं बभञ्ज परवीरहा ॥ 3 ॥
1.183.m:
he slew the Dānava named Mahiṣa, the thorn in the side of the gods; / and he slew tens of thousands of others equal in prowess to Mahiṣa.
When the heroic Skanda, crusher of enemy armies, was unable / to slay the Dānavas on account of their vast numbers, then the three-eyed god,
whose supreme weapon is the trident, slew [them] there with his mind, / and then slew other Dānavas by hundreds and by thousands.
Having struck down the hosts of the gods' enemies in battle, the Lord with three eyes, compassionate to devotees, / and having then caused the three worlds to rejoice, the great-souled one went to Mount Kailāsa.
1.234 / Nāḍāyana said: / Hear another display of power of that very god of gods: / formerly, when no share in the sacrifice was designated for the three-eyed one
by the gods wishing to sacrifice, O king, then by the enraged Śambhu, / having gone to the sacrificial enclosure, the gods were violently terrified.
Having devoured the sacrificial cake, he knocked out the teeth of Pūṣan; / the slayer of enemy heroes broke the left eye of Bhaga.

1.183.d:
क्रुद्धं दृष्ट्वा महादेवं मृगरूपधरस्तदा ॥
प्राद्रवत्सहसा यज्ञो नरनारायणाश्रमम् ॥ 4 ॥
तमन्वयो महातेजा बाणचापधरो हरः ॥
यज्ञानुसारिणं प्राप्तं हरं बाणधनुर्धरम् ॥ 5 ॥
नारायणस्तु तं चक्रे विह्वलं कण्ठपीडनात् ॥
विह्वले तु महादेवे यज्ञो दिवमथाश्रितः ॥ 6 ॥
हरोऽपि लब्धसंज्ञस्तमन्वयौ दिवि सत्त्वरः ॥
न शशाक मृगं वेद्धुं यदा धर्मश्च तेजसा ॥ 7 ॥
ततस्तं बोधयामास ब्रह्मा शुभचतुर्मुखः ॥
भगस्य पूर्णं च तदा प्रसादमकरोत्पुनः ॥ 8 ॥
यज्ञस्य चाभयं दत्त्वा क्रीडयान्वेति तं पुनः ॥
तारामृगश्च गगने महादेवानुगः सदा ॥ 9 ॥
दृश्यते स महाभाग रात्रौ गगनभूषणः ॥1.234.10॥
क्रुद्धेन रुद्रेण सुरा निरस्ताः स्वस्थाः प्रसन्नेन कृताश्च भूयः ॥
तस्मात्प्रसन्नास्तु भवाय लोके क्रुद्धश्च लोकान्तकरः प्रदिष्टः ॥ 11 ॥
1.183.m:
Seeing Mahādeva enraged, the Sacrifice, taking the form of a deer, / then fled at once to the hermitage of Nara and Nārāyaṇa.
Hara of great splendour, holding bow and arrows, pursued it. / When Hara arrived, holding bow and arrows and pursuing the Sacrifice,
Nārāyaṇa threw him into confusion by seizing his throat. / While Mahādeva was in distress, the Sacrifice then took refuge in heaven.
Hara, too, regaining consciousness, quickly pursued it in heaven. / When Dharma, by his splendour, could not pierce the deer,
then Brahmā, auspicious and four-faced, enlightened him. / Then he granted complete favour once again to Bhaga,
and granting safety to the Sacrifice, he playfully pursued it again. / And the star-deer in the sky, ever following Mahādeva,
is seen at night as an ornament of the sky, O fortunate one.
When enraged, Rudra cast down the gods, and when pleased, he restored them once again; / therefore, when pleased he leads to welfare in the world, and when enraged he is declared the destroyer of the worlds.

॥ नाडायन उवाच ॥
तस्यैव देवदेवस्य प्रभावमपरं शृणु ॥
तेन विध्वंसितो यज्ञो यदा दक्षस्य धीमतः ॥ 1 ॥
दक्षस्य यजमानस्य गङ्गाद्वारे पुरा प्रभो ॥
अनाह्वाने च शर्वस्य देवीप्रकुपिताऽभवत ॥ 2 ॥
देव्याः प्रकोपाच्च तथा क्रुद्धः शूलधरस्तदा ॥
वीरभद्रेति विख्यातं क्रोधजं सृष्टवान्गणम् ॥ 3 ॥
भद्रकाली स्वकाद्देहात्सृष्टवत्यथ पार्वती ॥
गणैरनुगतो राजन्वीरभद्रो महायशाः ॥ 4 ॥
भद्रकालीं तथा गत्वा दक्षयज्ञमशातयत् ॥
विध्वस्यमानं यज्ञन्तु पार्वत्या सहितः शिवः ॥ 5 ॥
दृष्टवांस्तत्र राजेन्द्र भद्रकर्णेश्वरः स्थितः ॥
विध्वस्यमाने यज्ञे तु दक्षो वचनमब्रवीत् ॥ 6 ॥
1.183.m:
Thus ends the two hundred and thirty-fourth chapter, entitled “The Destruction of the Sacrifice,” in the first book of the venerable Viṣṇudharmottara in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra.
1.235 / Nāḍāyana said: / Hear another display of power of that very god of gods: / when the sacrifice of the wise Dakṣa was destroyed by him,
when Dakṣa was sacrificing long ago at Gaṅgādvāra, O lord, / because Śarva was not invited, the Goddess became enraged.
And on account of the Goddess’s fury, the wielder of the trident was then enraged, / and created an attendant known as Vīrabhadra, born of his anger.
Then Pārvatī created Bhadrakālī from her own body. / Accompanied by the attendants, O king, the renowned Vīrabhadra,
together with Bhadrakālī, went and destroyed Dakṣa's sacrifice. / And Śiva, accompanied by Pārvatī,
beholding the sacrifice being destroyed, remained there as Bhadrakarṇeśvara, O lord of kings. / But while the sacrifice was being destroyed, Dakṣa spoke these words

क्रुद्धेन शङ्करेणावां भागस्यापरिकल्पनात् ॥

भद्रकर्णेश्वरं शर्वं गच्छ शीघ्रं प्रसादय ॥
नाडायन उवाच ॥
वीरभद्रवचः श्रुत्वा गत्वा तुष्टाव शङ्करम् ॥ 9 ॥
अश्वमेधसहस्राग्र्यं फलं लेभे त्रिलोचनात् ॥
त्रिलोचनस्तदा तुष्टो वीरभद्रमभाषत ॥ 1.235.10 ॥
यत्रस्थेन त्वया यज्ञो दक्षस्याद्य विनाशितः ॥
तत्र स्थाने तु सततं सान्निध्यं त्वं करिष्यसि ॥ 11 ॥
पूजां च विपुलां तत्र प्रास्प्यसे मत्प्रसादजाम् ॥
ये च त्वां पूजयिष्यन्ति वीरभद्र गणेश्वर ॥ 12 ॥
ते नाकपृष्ठं यास्यन्ति नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
दक्षेण च समाहूता भद्रकर्णेश्वरे त्वया ॥ 13 ॥
1.183.m:
to the highly fortunate Vīrabhadra and likewise to Bhadrakālī: / “Who are you two who have arrived here to ruin my sacrifice?”
Vīrabhadra said: / “By enraged Śaṅkara, because no share was designated, / we two, destroyers of foes, have been sent for the destruction of the sacrifice.
Go quickly and propitiate Śarva, the lord of Bhadrakarṇa.” / Nāḍāyana said: / Having heard Vīrabhadra's words, he went and praised Śaṅkara.
He obtained from the three-eyed one the reward surpassing a thousand horse-sacrifices. / The three-eyed one, being then pleased, spoke to Vīrabhadra:
“Stationed where Dakṣa’s sacrifice was destroyed by you today, / in that place you shall constantly maintain your presence.
And there you will receive abundant worship born of my grace. / And those who worship you, O Vīrabhadra, lord of the troops,
will go to the vault of heaven; there should be no doubt in this matter. / And invited by Dakṣa, you [shall reside] at Bhadrakarṇeśvara.”

1.183.d:
सरस्वती महाभागा प्रविष्टा जाह्नवीजलम् ॥
सङ्गमे च तयोः स्नात्वा पूजां मम करिष्यति ॥ 14 ॥
यः पुमान्स गणेशत्वं मम प्राप्स्यत्यसंशयम्॥
गङ्गाद्वारं कुशावर्तं बिल्वकं नीलपर्वतम् ॥15॥
तथा कनखलं तीर्थं सर्वपापप्रमोचनम् ॥
भविष्यति महाभाग तथैव च मनोहरम् ॥ 16 ॥
प्रजापतेर्यज्ञभुवं समासाद्य यतस्ततः ॥
मोक्ष्यते पातकं सर्वं त्रिदिवं च गमिष्यति ॥ 17 ॥
भूमिष्ठमुद्धृतात्पुण्यं तस्मात्प्रस्रवणोदकम्॥
तस्मादपि तथा पुण्यं सारसं परिकीर्तितम् ॥
सारसान्नैर्झरं पुण्यं नादेयमपि नैर्झरात् ॥ 18॥
तस्मादपि च गाङ्गेयं तदिहापि विशेषतः ॥
सर्वत्र दुर्लभा गङ्गा त्रिषु स्थानेषु दुर्लभा॥.19॥
गङ्गाद्वारे प्रयागे च गङ्गासागरसङ्गमे॥
गङ्गाद्वारे कुशावर्त्ते बिल्वके नीलपर्वते ॥1.235.20॥
1.183.m:
The glorious Sarasvatī, having entered the waters of the Jāhnavī, / and bathing at their confluence, shall worship me.
Whatever person [does so], he will obtain leadership of my gaṇas, without doubt. / Gaṅgādvāra, Kuśāvarta, Bilvaka, Nīlaparvata,
and the sacred ford Kanakhala, which releases from all sins, / shall likewise be captivating, O illustrious one.
Having reached the sacrificial ground of the Prajāpati, by that very virtue / one will be freed from all sin and will go to heaven.
Water found in the ground is more meritorious than drawn [water], spring water is more meritorious than that; / lake water is declared even more meritorious than that; / waterfall water is more meritorious than lake water, and river water even more than waterfall water.
And the water of the Gaṅgā is even more [meritorious] than that, especially right here. / The Gaṅgā is rare everywhere, but hard to attain in three places:
at Gaṅgādvāra, at Prayāga, and at the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the ocean. / At Gaṅgādvāra, at Kuśāvarta, at Bilvaka, at Nīlaparvata,

स्नात्वा कनखले तीर्थे न पुनर्जन्मभाग्भवेत् ॥
तीर्थपञ्चकमेतद्धि यत्रैव गणनायकः ॥ 21 ॥
तत्र सन्निहितो ब्रह्मा तत्राहं तत्र केशवः ॥
तत्र देवगणाः सर्वे ऋषयश्च तपोधनाः ॥ 22 ॥
तत्समीपे च ते स्थानं त्विदं दत्तं मया तव ॥
तत्र त्वं सततं वत्स लोकात्पूजामवाप्स्यसि ॥ 23 ॥
एवमुक्त्वा महातेजा वीरभद्रं महेश्वरः ॥
उवाच वचनं देवो भद्रकालीं महेश्वरः ॥24 ॥
महेश्वर उवाच ॥
नमोस्तु ते महाभागे वरदे कामरूपिणि ॥
अष्टादशभुजे स्वस्ति शूलमुद्गरधारिणि ॥ 29 ॥
पीतकौशेयवसने शशाङ्कसदृशानने ॥
नीलोत्पलदलश्यामे गजकुम्भोपमस्तनि ॥ 26 ॥
वरदे चारुसर्वाङ्गि सर्वाभरणभूषिते॥
कमण्डलुधरे देवि देवारिबलनाशिनि॥27॥
अदितिश्च दितिश्चैव वनिता सिद्धिरेव च॥
रात्रिर्निद्रा प्रभा कान्तिर्बुद्धिर्लक्ष्मीः सरस्वती॥28॥
1.183.m:
having bathed at the sacred ford Kanakhala, one does not share in rebirth again. / For wherever this group of five sacred fords is, O leader of the gaṇas,
there Brahmā is present, there I am, and there is Keśava; / there are all the hosts of gods and the sages rich in austerity.
And near to that, this place has been given by me to you. / There, my child, you will constantly receive worship from the world.
Having spoken thus to the mighty Vīrabhadra, the great lord, / the divine Maheśvara addressed Bhadrakālī with these words:
Maheśvara said: / Homage to you, O illustrious one, boon-giver, who take forms at will! / Hail to you, eighteen-armed one, bearer of the trident and the club!
O you who wear yellow silken garments, whose face is like the moon, / dark as a blue lotus petal, whose breasts resemble the temples of an elephant!
O boon-giver, whose limbs are all lovely, adorned with all ornaments, / bearer of the water pot, O goddess, destroyer of the army of the gods' enemies!
You are Aditi, Diti, and womanhood, and perfection itself; / night, sleep, radiant light, beauty, intellect, Lakṣmī, Sarasvatī,

नवम्यां शुक्लपक्षस्य लोकात्पूजामवाप्स्यसि ॥
नवम्यां पूजयिष्यन्ति ये त्वा सम्यगुपोषिताः॥1.235.30॥
तेषां त्वं काम्यदा सौम्ये भविष्यसि न संशयः ॥
कन्दरेषु च शैलानां वनानां गहनेषु च ॥ 31 ॥
रंस्यसे त्वं विशालाक्षि तदा पूजामवाप्स्यसि ॥
ये च त्वां मत्प्रभावज्ञाः पूजयिष्यन्ति मानवाः ॥32॥
न तेषां दुर्लभं किञ्चिदिहलोके परत्र च ॥
ये चेदं मत्कृतं स्तोत्रमभिदास्यन्ति भक्तितः॥33॥
ते सर्वे भयनिर्मुक्ता भविष्यन्ति न संशयः ॥
नाडायन उवाच॥
एतावदुक्त्वा वचनं तत्रैवान्तरधीयत॥34॥
दक्षोपि च वरं लब्ध्वा मुदं लेभे त्रिलोचनात्॥35॥
1.183.m:
firmness, fame, the svadhā and the svāhā call—you alone are the woman of excellent complexion! / People will worship you, auspicious granter of all desires.
On the ninth day of the bright fortnight, you will receive worship from the world. / Those who, having fasted properly, worship you on the ninth day,
to them you will grant their desires, gentle one, without doubt. / And in the caves of mountains and the depths of forests,
you will delight, large-eyed one, and then you will receive worship. / And those mortals who, knowing my greatness, worship you,
for them nothing will be difficult to obtain in this world or in the next. / And those who recite with devotion this praise composed by me,
they will all be freed from fear, without doubt. / Nāḍāyana said: / Having spoken this speech, he vanished right there.
Dakṣa too, having obtained a boon from the three-eyed god, experienced joy.

रक्तवृत्तत्रिनयनः सर्पवृश्चिकरोमवान् ॥
दंष्ट्राकरालो विकटः चूर्णिताञ्जनसप्रभः ॥ 4 ॥
1.184.m: with three red and round eyes, hair like serpents and scorpions, / terrifying with fangs, monstrous, shining like crushed collyrium,

1.184.s:
raktavāsā mahākāyaḥ sarpābharaṇabhūṣitaḥ ..
pāśahastastathābhyetya śvete pāśamathāsṛjat .. 5 ..
1.184.d:
रक्तवासा महाकायः सर्पाभरणभूषितः ॥
पाशहस्तस्तथाभ्येत्य श्वेते पाशमथासृजत् ॥ 5 ॥
1.184.m: clothed in red, having a huge body, adorned with serpent ornaments, / with a noose in his hand; and approaching, he cast a noose upon Śveta.

1.184.s:
kaṇṭhārpitena pāśena śvetaḥ kālamathābravīt ..
kṣaṇamātraṃ pratīkṣasva mama tribhuvanāntaka .. 6 ..
1.184.d:
कण्ठार्पितेन पाशेन श्वेतः कालमथाब्रवीत् ॥
क्षणमात्रं प्रतीक्षस्व मम त्रिभुवनान्तक ॥ 6 ॥
1.184.m: With the noose fastened around his throat, Śveta then spoke to Time: / "Wait for just a moment for me, O ender of the three worlds,

1.184.s:
nivarttayāmyahaṃ yāvatpūjanaṃ manmathadviṣaḥ ..
tamabravīttadā kālaḥ prahasanvasudhādhipa .. 7 ..
1.184.d:
निवर्त्तयाम्यहं यावत्पूजनं मन्मथद्विषः ॥
तमब्रवीत्तदा कालः प्रहसन्वसुधाधिप ॥ 7 ॥
1.184.m: while I complete my worship of the enemy of Manmatha!" / Then Time laughed and spoke to him, O ruler of the earth:

1.184.s:
na śrutaṃ tu tvayā manye vṛddhānāṃ śveta jalpitam ..
śvaḥ kāryamadya kurvīta pūrvāhṇe cāparāhṇike .. 8 ..
1.184.d:
न श्रुतं तु त्वया मन्ये वृद्धानां श्वेत जल्पितम् ॥
श्वः कार्यमद्य कुर्वीत पूर्वाह्णे चापराह्णिके ॥ 8 ॥
1.184.m: "I think you have not heard the saying of the elders, Śveta: / One should do today the work of tomorrow, and in the forenoon that of the afternoon.

1.184.s:
na hi pratīkṣate mṛtyuḥ kṛtaṃ vā syānna vā kṛtam ..
garbhe vāpyatha bālye vā yauvane vārdhakepi vā .. 9 ..
1.184.d:
न हि प्रतीक्षते मृत्युः कृतं वा स्यान्न वा कृतम् ॥
गर्भे वाप्यथ बाल्ये वा यौवने वार्धकेपि वा ॥ 9 ॥
1.184.m: For Death does not wait [to see] whether it has been done or not done. / Either in the womb, or in childhood, in youth or in old age,

1.184.s:
āyuṣye karmaṇi kṣīṇe loko'yaṃ nīyate mayā ..
nauṣadhāni na maṃtrāśca na homo na punarjapaḥ .. 1.236.10 ..
1.184.d:
आयुष्ये कर्मणि क्षीणे लोकोऽयं नीयते मया ॥
नौषधानि न मंत्राश्च न होमो न पुनर्जपः ॥ 1.236.10 ॥
1.184.m: when one's lifespan and karma are exhausted, this person is carried away by me. / Neither medicines nor mantras, neither fire-offerings nor repeated recitations

1.184.s:
trāyanti mṛtyunopetṃ jarayā vāpi mānavam ..
bahūnīndrasahasrāṇi pitāmahaśatāni ca .. 11 ..
1.184.d:
त्रायन्ति मृत्युनोपेत्ं जरया वापि मानवम् ॥
बहूनीन्द्रसहस्राणि पितामहशतानि च ॥ 11 ॥
1.184.m: protect a mortal who has been approached by Death or by old age. / Many thousands of Indras and hundreds of Grandfathers

1.184.s:
mayā nītāni karttavyo nātra manyustvayānagha ..
vidhatse pūjanaṃ yasya mahādevasya śūlinaḥ .. 12 ..
1.184.d:
मया नीतानि कर्त्तव्यो नात्र मन्युस्त्वयानघ ॥
विधत्से पूजनं यस्य महादेवस्य शूलिनः ॥ 12 ॥
1.184.m: have been carried off by me; you must not feel anger at this, sinless one. / That Mahādeva, the trident-bearer, whose worship you perform—

1.184.s:
dehanyāsaṃ sa bahudhā mayā vai śveta kāritaḥ ..
svayaṃ prabhurna caivāhaṃ karmāyattā matirmama .. 13 ..
1.184.d:
देहन्यासं स बहुधा मया वै श्वेत कारितः ॥
स्वयं प्रभुर्न चैवाहं कर्मायत्ता मतिर्मम ॥ 13 ॥
1.184.m: the abandonment of the body was brought about for him by me many times, Śveta. / I am not my own master; my purpose is dependent on karma.

1.184.s:
karmaṇāṃ hi tathā nāśaṃ nāsti bhūtasya kasyacit ..
karmamārgānusāreṇa dhātrāhaṃ saṃpracoditaḥ .. 14 ..
1.184.d:
कर्मणां हि तथा नाशं नास्ति भूतस्य कस्यचित् ॥
कर्ममार्गानुसारेण धात्राहं संप्रचोदितः ॥ 14 ॥
1.184.m: For there is no destruction of actions for any being whatsoever. / Urged on by the Creator according to the path of karma,

1.184.s:
nayāmi sarvamākramya trailokyaṃ sacarācaram ..
evamuktastu kālena nīyamānastrilocanam .. 15 ..
1.184.d:
नयामि सर्वमाक्रम्य त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम् ॥
एवमुक्तस्तु कालेन नीयमानस्त्रिलोचनम् ॥ 15 ॥
1.184.m: I overpower and take away the entire triple world, with its moving and unmoving beings." / Thus addressed by Time and being led away, towards the three-eyed god

1.184.s:
jagāma sarvabhāvena śaraṇaṃ bhaktavatsalam ..
śvete tu śaraṇaṃ prāpte liṅgasya tripurāntakaḥ .. 16 ..
1.184.d:
जगाम सर्वभावेन शरणं भक्तवत्सलम् ॥
श्वेते तु शरणं प्राप्ते लिङ्गस्य त्रिपुरान्तकः ॥ 16 ॥
1.184.m: he went for refuge with his whole being, [to the one] who is affectionate to devotees. / When Śveta took refuge in the liṅga, the destroyer of Tripura,

1.184.s:
bhūtabhavyabhaviṣyadbhiḥ prādurbhāvaistu śārṅgiṇaḥ ..
ātmanaḥ kavacaṃ kṛttvā kṛtarakṣo maheśvaraḥ .. 17 ..
1.184.d:
भूतभव्यभविष्यद्भिः प्रादुर्भावैस्तु शार्ङ्गिणः ॥
आत्मनः कवचं कृत्त्वा कृतरक्षो महेश्वरः ॥ 17 ॥
1.184.m: making an armor for himself with the past, present, and future manifestations of the wielder of the bow Śārṅga, his protection secured, Maheśvara

1.184.s:
bhittvā liṅgaṃ samuttasthau krodhavisphāritekṣaṇaḥ ..
tṛtīyalocanajvālāprakāśitajagattrayaḥ ..18..
1.184.d:
भित्त्वा लिङ्गं समुत्तस्थौ क्रोधविस्फारितेक्षणः ॥
तृतीयलोचनज्वालाप्रकाशितजगत्त्रयः ॥18॥
1.184.m: burst through the liṅga and rose up, his eyes wide with fury, / illuminating the three worlds with the flame of his third eye.

1.184.s:
dṛṣṭamātrastadā tasya kālo jajvāla tejasā ..
sa śānto bhasmabhūtaśca sarvabhūtavidhirgrahaḥ .. 19 ..
1.184.d:
दृष्टमात्रस्तदा तस्य कालो जज्वाल तेजसा ॥
स शान्तो भस्मभूतश्च सर्वभूतविधिर्ग्रहः ॥ 19 ॥
1.184.m: As soon as he was seen, Time blazed up with his radiance; / and he was extinguished and turned to ash, he who was the seizer and the ordainer of all beings.

1.184.s:
śvetasya dattvā sāmīpyaṃ gaṇeśatvaṃ tathaiva ca ..
kṛtvā vidhigrahaṃ kālaṃ tatraivāntaradhīyata .. 1.236.20 ..
1.184.d:
श्वेतस्य दत्त्वा सामीप्यं गणेशत्वं तथैव च ॥
कृत्वा विधिग्रहं कालं तत्रैवान्तरधीयत ॥ 1.236.20 ॥
1.184.m: Having granted Śveta proximity to himself as well as the status of a lord of gaṇas, / and having made Time a controller by rule, he vanished right there.

1.184.s:
tataḥ prabhṛti rājendra kālaḥ sa kalayanprajām..
na kaiściddṛśyate loke videhatvājjagattraye ..21 ..
1.184.d:
ततः प्रभृति राजेन्द्र कालः स कलयन्प्रजाम्॥
न कैश्चिद्दृश्यते लोके विदेहत्वाज्जगत्त्रये ॥21 ॥
1.184.m: From that time forward, O king of kings, that Time, driving creatures on, / is not seen by anyone in the world in the three worlds because of being bodiless.

1.184.s:
.. śailūṣa uvāca .. ..
vaiṣṇavaṃ kavacaṃ brahmansarvabādhānivāraṇam ..
tvattohaṃ śrotumicchāmi tatra me saṃśayo mahān .. 22 ..
1.184.d:
॥ शैलूष उवाच ॥ ॥
वैष्णवं कवचं ब्रह्मन्सर्वबाधानिवारणम् ॥
त्वत्तोहं श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्र मे संशयो महान् ॥ 22 ॥
1.184.m: Śailūṣa said: / O brahmin, I wish to hear from you the Vaiṣṇava armour / which wards off all afflictions; regarding that, I have great doubt.

1.184.s:
.. nāḍāyana uvāca ..
adṛśyametatparamaṃ pavitraṃ pūrveritaṃ kalmaṣanāśanaṃ ca ..
duḥkhāpahaṃ te kavacaṃ bravīmi rakṣā kṛtā yena maheśvareṇa .. 23 ..
1.237
.. maheśvara uvāca .. ..
praṇamyājaramīśānamajaṃ nityamanāmayam ..
devaṃ sarveśvaraṃ viṣṇuṃ sarvavyāpinamavyayam .. 1 ..
badhnāmyahaṃ pratisaraṃ namaskṛtya janārddanam ..
amoghamapratihataṃ sarvaduḥṣṭanivāraṇam .. 2 ..
viṣṇurmamāgrataḥ pātu kṛṣṇo rakṣatu pṛṣṭhataḥ ..
harirme rakṣatu śiro hṛdayaṃ ca janārddanaḥ .. 3 ..
mano mama hṛṣīkeśo jihvāṃ rakṣatu keśavaḥ..
pātu netre vāsudevaḥ śrotre saṃkarṣaṇastathā .. 4 ..
pradyumnaḥ pātu me ghrāṇamaniruddho mukhaṃ mama ..
vanamālī galaṃ pātu śrīvakṣo rakṣatātpuraḥ ..
pārśvaṃ tu pātu me cakraṃ vāmaṃ daityavidāraṇam .. 5 ..
1.184.d:
॥ नाडायन उवाच ॥
अदृश्यमेतत्परमं पवित्रं पूर्वेरितं कल्मषनाशनं च ॥
दुःखापहं ते कवचं ब्रवीमि रक्षा कृता येन महेश्वरेण ॥ 23 ॥
1.237
॥ महेश्वर उवाच ॥ ॥
प्रणम्याजरमीशानमजं नित्यमनामयम् ॥
देवं सर्वेश्वरं विष्णुं सर्वव्यापिनमव्ययम् ॥ 1 ॥
बध्नाम्यहं प्रतिसरं नमस्कृत्य जनार्द्दनम् ॥
अमोघमप्रतिहतं सर्वदुःष्टनिवारणम् ॥ 2 ॥
विष्णुर्ममाग्रतः पातु कृष्णो रक्षतु पृष्ठतः ॥
हरिर्मे रक्षतु शिरो हृदयं च जनार्द्दनः ॥ 3 ॥
मनो मम हृषीकेशो जिह्वां रक्षतु केशवः॥
पातु नेत्रे वासुदेवः श्रोत्रे संकर्षणस्तथा ॥ 4 ॥
प्रद्युम्नः पातु मे घ्राणमनिरुद्धो मुखं मम ॥
वनमाली गलं पातु श्रीवक्षो रक्षतात्पुरः ॥
पार्श्वं तु पातु मे चक्रं वामं दैत्यविदारणम् ॥ 5 ॥
1.184.m:
Nāḍāyana said: / Invisible, supreme, pure, proclaimed of old and destroying sin, / removing sorrow is the armour I speak to you of, by which protection was made by Maheśvara.
1.237 / Maheśvara said: / Having bowed to the unaging, the sovereign, unborn, eternal, free from disease, / the god who is the Lord of All, Viṣṇu, all-pervading and imperishable,
having bowed to Janārdana, I bind the protective amulet, / unfailing, unobstructed, warding off all wicked things.
May Viṣṇu protect in front of me; may Kṛṣṇa guard behind. / May Hari guard my head, and Janārdana my heart.
May Hṛṣīkeśa protect my mind; may Keśava guard my tongue. / May Vāsudeva protect my eyes, and Saṃkarṣaṇa my ears.
May Pradyumna protect my nose, and Aniruddha my mouth. / May he who wears a forest garland protect my throat; may the Śrīvatsa-chested protect in front; / and may the discus, the tearer of Daityas, protect my left side;

1.184.s:
dakṣiṇaṃ tu gadā devī sarvāsuranivāriṇī ..
udaraṃ musalī pātu pṛṣṭhaṃ pātu ca lāṅgalī .. 6 ..
ūrū rakṣatu śārṅgī me jaṅghe rakṣatu carmakī ..
pāṇī rakṣatu śaṃkhī ca pādau me caraṇāvubhau ..
sarvakāryārthasiddhyarthaṃ pātu māṃ garuḍadhvajaḥ ..7..
varāho rakṣatu jale viṣameṣu ca vāmanaḥ ..
aṭavyāṃ narasiṃhastu sarvataḥ pātu keśavaḥ .. 8 ..
hiraṇyagarbho bhagavānhiraṇyaṃ me prayacchatu ..
sāṃkhyācāryastu kapilo dhātusāmyaṃ karotu me .. 9 ..
śvetadvīpanivāsī ca śvetadvīpaṃ nayatvajaḥ ..
sarvāñśatrūnsūdayatu madhukaiṭabhasūdanaḥ .. 1.237.10 ..
vikarṣatu sadā viṣṇuḥ kilbiṣaṃ mama vigrahāt ..
haṃso matsyastathā kūrmaḥ pātu māṃ sarvato diśam .. 11 ..
trivikramastu me devaḥ sarvānpāśānnikṛntatu ..
naranārāyaṇo devo buddhiṃ pālayatāṃ mama .. 12 ..
1.184.d:
दक्षिणं तु गदा देवी सर्वासुरनिवारिणी ॥
उदरं मुसली पातु पृष्ठं पातु च लाङ्गली ॥ 6 ॥
ऊरू रक्षतु शार्ङ्गी मे जङ्घे रक्षतु चर्मकी ॥
पाणी रक्षतु शंखी च पादौ मे चरणावुभौ ॥
सर्वकार्यार्थसिद्ध्यर्थं पातु मां गरुडध्वजः ॥7॥
वराहो रक्षतु जले विषमेषु च वामनः ॥
अटव्यां नरसिंहस्तु सर्वतः पातु केशवः ॥ 8 ॥
हिरण्यगर्भो भगवान्हिरण्यं मे प्रयच्छतु ॥
सांख्याचार्यस्तु कपिलो धातुसाम्यं करोतु मे ॥ 9 ॥
श्वेतद्वीपनिवासी च श्वेतद्वीपं नयत्वजः ॥
सर्वाञ्शत्रून्सूदयतु मधुकैटभसूदनः ॥ 1.237.10 ॥
विकर्षतु सदा विष्णुः किल्बिषं मम विग्रहात् ॥
हंसो मत्स्यस्तथा कूर्मः पातु मां सर्वतो दिशम् ॥ 11 ॥
त्रिविक्रमस्तु मे देवः सर्वान्पाशान्निकृन्ततु ॥
नरनारायणो देवो बुद्धिं पालयतां मम ॥ 12 ॥
1.184.m:
and the divine club, warding off all Asuras, my right [side]. / May the wielder of the pestle protect my belly, and the wielder of the plough my back.
May the wielder of the bow Śārṅga guard my thighs; may the wielder of the shield guard my shanks. / May the wielder of the conch guard my hands, and both my feet, my two limbs. / For the accomplishment of all aims and tasks, may he whose banner is Garuḍa protect me.
May the Boar protect in water, and the Dwarf in rough places. / In the forest, indeed, Narasiṃha; and may Keśava protect on every side.
May the blessed Hiraṇyagarbha bestow gold upon me; / and may Kapila, the teacher of Sāṃkhya, effect equilibrium of my bodily humours.
And may the unborn dweller in Śvetadvīpa lead [me] to Śvetadvīpa. / May the slayer of Madhu and Kaiṭabha destroy all enemies.
May Viṣṇu ever pull away sin from my body. / May the Swan, the Fish, and the Tortoise protect me in every direction.
May the god Trivikrama sever all my fetters; / may the god Nara-Nārāyaṇa preserve my intellect.

1.184.s:
śeṣo śeṣāmalajñānaḥ karotvajñānanāśanam ..
vaḍavāmukho nāśayatu kalmaṣaṃ yanmayā kṛtam .. 13 ..
vidyāṃ dadātu paramāmaśvamūrddhā mama prabhuḥ ..
dattātreyaḥ pālayatu saputrapaśubāndhavam .. 14 ..
sarvānrogānnāśayatu rāmaḥ paraśunā mama ..
rakṣoghno me dāśarathiḥ pātu nityaṃ mahābhujaḥ .. 15 ..
ripūnhalena me hanyādrāmo yādavanandanaḥ ..
pralambakeśicāṇūrapūtanākaṃsanāśanaḥ .. 16 ..
kṛṣṇo yo bālabhāvena sa me kāmānprayacchatu ..
andhakāraṃ tamo ghoraṃ puruṣaṃ kṛṣṇapiṅgalam .. 17 ..
paśyāmi bhayasaṃtaptaḥ pāśahastamivāntakam..
tato'haṃ puṇḍarīkākṣamacyutaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ .. 18 ..
yogīśamatirūpasthaṃ śubhaśītāṃśunirmalam ..
dhanyo'haṃ vijayī nityaṃ yasya me bhagavānhariḥ .. 19 ..
smṛtvā nārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ sarvopadravanāśanam ..
vaiṣṇavaṃ kavacaṃ baddhvā vicarāmi mahītale .. 1.237.20 ..
1.184.d:
शेषो शेषामलज्ञानः करोत्वज्ञाननाशनम् ॥
वडवामुखो नाशयतु कल्मषं यन्मया कृतम् ॥ 13 ॥
विद्यां ददातु परमामश्वमूर्द्धा मम प्रभुः ॥
दत्तात्रेयः पालयतु सपुत्रपशुबान्धवम् ॥ 14 ॥
सर्वान्रोगान्नाशयतु रामः परशुना मम ॥
रक्षोघ्नो मे दाशरथिः पातु नित्यं महाभुजः ॥ 15 ॥
रिपून्हलेन मे हन्याद्रामो यादवनन्दनः ॥
प्रलम्बकेशिचाणूरपूतनाकंसनाशनः ॥ 16 ॥
कृष्णो यो बालभावेन स मे कामान्प्रयच्छतु ॥
अन्धकारं तमो घोरं पुरुषं कृष्णपिङ्गलम् ॥ 17 ॥
पश्यामि भयसंतप्तः पाशहस्तमिवान्तकम्॥

स्मृत्वा नारायणं देवं सर्वोपद्रवनाशनम् ॥
वैष्णवं कवचं बद्ध्वा विचरामि महीतले ॥ 1.237.20 ॥
1.184.m:
May Śeṣa, possessing boundless pure knowledge, destroy [my] ignorance. / May the Submarine Fire destroy the stain that has been done by me.
May the horse-headed Lord grant supreme knowledge to me; / may Dattātreya protect [me] together with sons, livestock, and kin.
May Rāma with his axe destroy all diseases of mine; / may the son of Daśaratha, slayer of Rakṣasas, mighty-armed, ever protect me.
May Rāma, delight of the Yādavas, strike down my foes with his plough; / he who slew Pralamba, Keśin, Cāṇūra, Pūtanā, and Kaṃsa,
Kṛṣṇa who was in the state of a child, may he grant my desires. / Deep darkness, dreadful gloom, a dark and reddish-brown person,
I see, tormented by fear, like Death with a noose in his hand. / Thereupon I have gone for refuge to the lotus-eyed, unfalling one,
the Lord of Yogins abiding in transcendent form, spotless as the auspicious cool-rayed [moon]. / Blessed am I, ever victorious, whose [protector] is the Blessed Hari.
Remembering the god Nārāyaṇa, the destroyer of all calamities, / having bound on the Vaiṣṇava armour, I wander upon the surface of the earth.

1.184.m: Svāhā to time! / Svāhā to the person of time! / Svāhā to the fierce one! / Svāhā to the fierce person! / Svāhā to the All! / Svāhā to the All of All! / Oṃ, reverence to the Lord of the world, whose abode is the three worlds: itiṭi piriṭi svāhā! / Oṃ, by the highest […] for me, O wind, for me; whatever beings walk in evil—among them daityas, dānavas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, pretas, piśācas, kūṣmāṇḍas, apasmāras, lunacy, and the fevers: quotidian, tertian, quartan, four-day, hourly, day-fever, night-fever, continuous fever, twilight fever, and the destruction of all fevers and the rest; spiders, insects, thorns, kaṭapūtanās, serpents, stationary poisons, virulent poisons, and the rest—may this body of mine be invincible! Oṃ, with a good syllable, he acts: fierce, terrible-fanged one, protect from the east! / Oṃ haiṃ haiṃ haiṃ haiṃ, fierce brilliance equal to the radiance of a thousand suns, protect, protect from the west! / Oṃ, blazing fire in burning flames, black with time, great yellow-haired ascetic with matted locks, protect from the north! / Oṃ cilicili milimili cekaḍi gauri gāndhāri poison-destroyer, may poison bewilder me, svāhā! / Protect me, [insert name], from the south, from the dangers and afflictions of all beings, svāhā! / Victory triumphs, may the grant of victory arise! The destroyer of enemy cities does not strike; dispelling fear from the heart, bestowing fear, may this noble Acyuta grant fearlessness to fear! / Into whose belly all rays enter, / having beginning and end, the ancient seers, subtle, immense, the rulers— / may Aniruddha, Pradyumna, Saṃkarṣaṇa, and Vāsudeva destroy all fevers for me!

1.184.m:
1.238 / Vajra said: / Having heard the burning of Kālāṅga spoken by the brahmin, / what did Śailūṣa, driven by death, then ask, O holy one?
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Having heard the burning of Kālāṅga spoken by the brahmin, / he then asked him again about the deeds of Rāvaṇa alone.
Śailūṣa said: / What remains of the deeds of the ten-necked rākṣasa, / that I wish to hear; I have great doubt about it.
Nāḍāyana said: / Then Rāvaṇa walked all around his city once more. / He then saw there an entirely golden mansion,
surrounded by nets of pearls, with arches of coral, / and with an altar made entirely of emerald and ruby,
with beautiful pillars of lapis lazuli, blazing with the lustre of rubies, / covered with the radiance of sapphires, adorned with hundreds of turrets,
crowded with great halls, adorned with a great garden, / having stairs easy to ascend, filled with hundreds of oblong ponds,

सर्वर्तु कुसुमैर्वृक्षैः समन्तादुपशोभितम् ॥
सर्वासनयुतं रम्यं महेन्द्रभवनाधिकम ॥ 8 ॥
तन्तु दृष्ट्वा गृहं राजन्प्रहस्तं वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥
प्रहस्त शीघ्रं जानीहि कस्येदं भवनोत्तमम् ॥ 9 ॥
एवमुक्तः प्रहस्तस्तु प्रविवेश गृहोत्तमम् ॥
संप्राप्तायां च कक्षायां भिन्नाञ्जनचयोपमम् ॥1.238.10 ॥
सर्वाभरणसंवीतं सर्वलक्षणलक्षितम् ॥
गृहीत्वा लोहमुसलं द्वारदेशे व्यवस्थितम् ॥ 11 ॥
ददर्श पुरुषं भीमं ज्वालामण्डलदुर्दृशम् ॥
तं तु दृष्ट्वा तथाभूतं स विवेश दशाननः ॥ 12 ॥
समाप्तायां च कक्षायां स ददर्श तमेव हि ॥
तमुवाच महातेजा निशाचरगणेश्वरः ॥ 13 ॥
युद्धार्थ्यहमनुप्राप्तो युद्धातिथ्यं प्रयच्छ मे ॥
अथ वा तस्य शंस त्वं गृहे योस्मिन्व्यवस्थितः ॥ 14 ॥
1.184.m:
beautified on all sides by trees blossoming in all seasons, / furnished with all kinds of seats, delightful, surpassing the mansion of Mahendra.
Seeing that house, O king, he spoke these words to Prahasta: / 'Prahasta, find out quickly whose excellent mansion this is!'
Addressed thus, Prahasta entered the excellent house. / And reaching the courtyard, [he saw one] resembling a heap of crushed collyrium,
covered with all kinds of ornaments, marked with all auspicious marks, / holding an iron club, standing at the doorway.
He saw a terrifying person, difficult to gaze upon like an orb of flames. / Seeing him in that condition, the ten-faced one entered.
And entering the courtyard, he saw that very same [person]. / The lord of the hosts of night-wanderers, full of great splendour, said to him:
'Desiring a battle, I have arrived: give me hospitality in the form of a fight! / Or tell me of the one who resides in this house!'

śīghramutsaṅgamāropya pṛṣṭastvāgamanaṃ tataḥ .. 19 ..
tasyovāca mahātejā rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ ..
śrutaṃ mayā mahābhāga baddhastvaṃ kila viṣṇunā .. 1.238.20 ..
so'haṃ mocayituṃ śakto bandhanāttvāṃ na saṃśayaḥ ..
evamuktastato hāsaṃ balirmuktvedamabravīt .. 21 ..
1.184.d:
ततो राक्षसराजस्य पुरुषो वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥
तिष्ठत्यस्मिन्गृहे राजा दानवानां बलिर्बली ॥ 15 ॥
तेन चेद्योत्स्यसे वीर प्रविशेदं गृहोत्तमम् ॥
योद्धुं नार्हसि तेन त्वं स महात्मा महाबलः ॥ 16 ॥
ब्रह्मण्यश्च शरण्यश्च शूरः सत्यपराक्रमः ॥
वीरो बहुगुणोपेतो बलवान्दृढविक्रमः ॥
बालार्क इव तेजस्वी समरेष्वनिवर्त्तकः ॥ 17 ॥
प्रियंवदः संविभागी गूढ साक्ष्याय तत्परः ॥
एवमुक्तो दशग्रीवः प्रविवेश गृहोत्तमम् ॥ 18 ॥
अथ संदर्शनादेव बलिना सुमहात्मना ॥
शीघ्रमुत्सङ्गमारोप्य पृष्टस्त्वागमनं ततः ॥ 19 ॥
तस्योवाच महातेजा रावणो राक्षसाधिपः ॥
श्रुतं मया महाभाग बद्धस्त्वं किल विष्णुना ॥ 1.238.20 ॥
सोऽहं मोचयितुं शक्तो बन्धनात्त्वां न संशयः ॥
एवमुक्तस्ततो हासं बलिर्मुक्त्वेदमब्रवीत् ॥ 21 ॥
1.184.m:
Then the person spoke these words to the king of the rākṣasas: / 'In this house dwells the king of the dānavas, mighty Bali.
If you would fight with him, O hero, enter this excellent house; / [yet] you should not fight with him: he is great-souled and possesses great strength.
He is devoted to brahmins, a refuge, heroic, of true valour, / brave, endowed with many virtues, strong, of firm prowess, / radiant like the morning sun, never retreating in battles,
pleasant-spoken, sharing [with others], devoted to secret witness.' / Addressed thus, the ten-necked one entered the excellent house.
Then, at the very sight [of him], the great-souled Bali, / having quickly placed him upon his lap, questioned him about his arrival.
To him the lord of the rākṣasas, Rāvaṇa, endowed with great splendour, said: / 'I have heard, O fortunate one, that you were bound by Viṣṇu.
I am capable of releasing you from bonds, of this there is no doubt.' / Addressed thus, Bali gave a laugh and said this:

1.184.d:
एते मे कुण्डले दिव्ये महारत्नोपशोभिते ॥
अनयोरेकमानीय चात्रोपविश मा चिरम् ॥ 22 ॥
अत्रोपविष्टस्य च ते व्याख्यास्ये विष्णुविक्रमम् ॥
एवमुक्तो दशग्रीवः कुण्डलानयने ततः॥23॥
चकार परमं यत्नं न शशाक च शत्रुहा ॥
यदा चालयितुं स्थानान्न शशाक स कुण्डलम् ॥ 24 ॥
प्रस्विन्नसर्वगात्रस्तु संदष्टदशनच्छदः ॥
भ्रकुटीसंकटमुखः परं विस्मयमागतः ॥ 25 ॥
उत्सङ्गे तदवस्थे तु बलिः कृत्वेदमब्रवीत् ॥
हिरण्यकशिपुर्नामाभवन्मे प्रपितामहः ॥ 26 ॥
यदा बभूव तस्येमे कुण्डले वै बभूवतुः ॥
एताभ्यां कुण्डलाभ्यां तु सोऽभूत्पूर्व विभूषितः ॥ 27 ॥
ऊर्वोरारोप्य नखरैः करैस्तेन विदारितः ॥
कथमद्य महाभागं तं त्वं जेतुं व्यवस्यसि ॥ 28 ॥
स एव पुरुषः श्यामो द्वारि तिष्ठति नित्यशः ॥
एतेन दानवेन्द्राश्च तथान्ये बलदर्पिताः ॥ 29॥
1.184.m:
'These are two divine earrings of mine, adorned with great gems; / having brought one of the two, sit here without delay.
And when you are seated here, I will explain to you the prowess of Viṣṇu.' / Addressed thus, the ten-necked one, that slayer of foes,
then made the supreme effort to bring the earring, but could not. / When he could not move the earring from its place,
his whole body sweating, his lips bitten by his teeth, / his face tight with a frown, he was filled with extreme astonishment.
Placing him in that condition on his lap, Bali said this: / 'There was a great-grandfather of mine named Hiraṇyakaśipu.
When he existed, these earrings indeed belonged to him; / with these two earrings he was formerly adorned.
Placed upon his thighs, he was torn apart by that [god] with the claws of his hands. / How do you now resolve to conquer that fortunate one?
That very dark person stands constantly at the doorway; / by him, the powerful one, lords of the dānavas and others proud of their strength,

बद्धश्चाहमनेनैव कालोऽयं दुरतिक्रमः ॥1.238.30 ॥
1.184.m: all who came earlier and earlier, were brought under control; / and I too was bound by him alone; this time is difficult to overcome.

लोकत्रयस्य सर्वस्य कर्ता हर्ता तथैव च ॥ 31 ॥
1.184.m: Who in this world can deceive this person, O rākṣasa? / He is the creator and likewise the destroyer of the entire three worlds.'

संहरत्येष भूतानि स्थावराणि चराणि च ॥
पुनश्च सृजते सर्वमनाद्यन्तो महेश्वरः ॥ 32 ॥
1.184.m: He destroys beings, both stationary and moving, / and creates everything again—the great Lord without beginning or end.

इष्टं चैव हुतं चैव तपस्तप्तं तथैव च ॥
सर्वस्येव हि लोकेशो धाता गोप्ता न संशयः ॥ 33 ॥
1.184.m: Whatever is offered in sacrifice, whatever is poured as oblation, and whatever austerity is performed, / of all this, indeed, the lord of the world is the ordainer and the protector; of this there is no doubt.

सर्वलोकमयश्चैव सर्वज्ञानमयस्तथा ॥ 34 ॥
1.184.m: He consists of all gods, and likewise of all beings; / he consists of all worlds, and likewise of all knowledge.

सर्वरूपी महारूपी महाबालो महाभुजः ॥
स्मृत्वा स्तुत्वा तथेष्ट्वा च सर्वमस्मादवाप्नुयात् ॥ 35 ॥
1.184.m: Having all forms, possessing a mighty form, endowed with great strength and mighty arms, / by remembering, praising, and sacrificing to him, one obtains everything from him.

1.184.m: And having heard these words, Rāvaṇa then departed; / and that night-roamer did not see that Cosmic Person there.

समेत्य रक्षोधिपतिः सहायश्चचार भूयः पृथिवीसमग्राम्॥

1.239
॥ नाडायन उवाच ॥ ॥
स कदाचिन्महीं सर्वां विचरन्धनदानुजः ॥
पश्चिमे सागरद्वीपे ददर्श पुरुषं शुभम् ॥ 1 ॥
जांबूनदसमप्रख्यं ज्वलितानलसुप्रभम् ॥
विश्वरूपधरं देवं वरदं कामरूपिणम् ॥ 2 ॥
धर्मस्तस्य तपश्चैव जगतः सिद्धिहेतुके ॥
ऊरू चाश्रित्य तस्थाते मन्मथः शिश्नमाश्रितः ॥ 3 ॥
विश्वेदेवाः कटीभागे मरुतो बस्तिशीर्षके ॥
पादयोश्च धरादेवी पिशाचाश्च नखाश्रिताः ॥ 4 ॥
मध्येष्टौ वसवस्तस्य समुद्राः कुक्षिमाश्रिताः ॥
पार्श्वेषु च दिशः सर्वाः सर्वस न्धिषु मारुतः ॥ 5 ॥
पितरश्चाश्रिताः पृष्ठे हृदये च पितामहः ॥
गोदानानि पवित्राणि भूमिदानानि यानि च ॥ 6 ॥
1.184.m:
Having met [him], the lord of the rākṣasas, together with his companions, wandered over the entire earth once more; / nor did that chief enemy of the gods see anyone else in the worlds who was steadfast.
1.239
Nāḍāyana said:
Once, while wandering across the entire earth, that younger brother of Dhanada / saw an auspicious person on an island in the western ocean,
resembling refined gold, shining brightly like blazing fire, / the god bearing a universal form, bestowing boons, assuming forms at will.
Dharma and austerity, which are the causes of success for the world, / resided resting upon his thighs; Love rested upon his penis.
The Viśvedevas were on his waist; the Maruts at the top of his bladder; / the goddess Earth was at his feet, and Piśācas rested on his nails.
In his middle were the eight Vasus; the oceans rested in his belly; / and in his sides were all the directions; the wind was in all his joints.
The ancestors rested upon his back, and the Grandfather in his heart; / the purifying gifts of cows and whatever gifts of land,

सुवर्णस्य च दानानि यकृल्लोमान्तराणि च ॥
अस्थिभागेषु शैलाश्च शिरासु सरितस्तथा ॥ 7 ॥
मणिवक्षोऽभवत्तस्य शरीरे द्यौरव स्थिता ॥
कृकाटिकायां सन्ध्याश्च तलवाहाश्च ये घनाः ॥ 8 ॥
बाहू धाता विधाता च भगः पूषा तथा करौ ॥
नागा घोरविषाः सर्वे करजेषु व्यवस्थियताः ॥ 9 ॥
अग्निरास्यमभूत्तस्य स्कन्धौ रुद्रैरधिष्ठितौ ॥
दन्ता मासर्तवश्चैव दंष्ट्रास्तस्य तु वत्सरः ॥ 1.239.10॥
नासायां चाप्यमावस्या तच्छि द्रेषु च वासराः ॥
ग्रीवा तस्याभवद्वेदी वाणी चाथ सरस्वती ॥ 11 ॥
नासत्यौ श्रवणौ चोभौ नेत्रे शशिदिवाकरौ ॥
वेदाङ्गानि च यज्ञाश्च तारा रूपाणि यानि च ॥ 12 ॥
एतानि नररूपस्य तस्य देहाश्रितानि वै ॥
तेनातिकायेन तदा राक्षसः पाणिपीडितः ॥13॥
मुमूर्च्छ सचिवाश्चास्या पलायन्त दिशो दश ॥
ऋग्वेदप्रतिमः श्रेष्ठः पद्ममालाविभूषितः ॥ 14 ॥
1.184.m:
and gifts of gold were between the hairs of his liver; / and in the parts of his bones were mountains, and likewise rivers in his blood vessels.
The sky was situated on his body with its jewelled breast; / the twilights were in his nape, as were the clouds that pour rain.
His two arms were Dhātṛ and Vidhātṛ; Bhaga and Pūṣan were his hands; / all serpents of terrible venom were situated in his fingernails.
Fire became his mouth; his shoulders were occupied by the Rudras; / his teeth were the months and the seasons, and his tusks were the year.
The new moon was in his nose, and the days were in its cavities; / his neck became the sacrificial altar, and Sarasvatī his speech.
Both the Nāsatyas were his ears; the sun and moon his eyes; / and the limbs of the Veda, the sacrifices, and whatever forms the stars have—
these indeed rested in the body of him who had human form. / Then, struck by the hand of that huge-bodied one, the rākṣasa
fainted, and his ministers fled in the ten directions. / Resembling the Ṛgveda, supreme, adorned with a garland of lotuses,

1.184.d:
क्रमेण च विवेशाथ पातालं गिरिसन्निभः ॥
उत्थाय च दशग्रीवश्चाहूय सचिवत्रयम्॥15॥
क्व गतः सहसा ब्रूत प्रहस्तशुकसारणाः॥
एवमुक्ते राक्षसेन्द्रे राक्षसास्तमथाब्रुवन्॥16॥
प्रविष्टः स नरोत्रैव देवदानवदर्पहा॥

एक एव महातेजा वरदानात्स्वयंभुवः ॥

एकरूपधरान्यर्वान्रक्तमाल्यानुलेपनान् ॥
रागद्वेषविनिर्मुक्तान्सर्वशक्तीञ्जगत्प्रभून् ॥ 1.239.20 ॥

1.184.m:
and resembling a mountain, he then gradually entered the underworld. / And the ten-necked one, having arisen and called his three ministers,
[said], “Where has he gone suddenly? Speak, Prahasta, Śuka, and Sāraṇa!” / When the lord of rākṣasas had spoken thus, the rākṣasas then said to him:
“That man who destroys the pride of gods and dānavas has entered right here.” / Then, through that very opening, the night-roamer entered.
Alone, endowed with great splendour because of the boon granted by the Self-born, / having entered, he saw there [beings] adorned with all ornaments,
in perpetual celebration, their fears calmed, partless, radiant as fire, / four-armed, of mighty forms, marked with the Śrīvatsa,
all bearing a single form, smeared with red ointments and wearing red garlands, / freed from attachment and aversion, having all powers, masters of the world,
serving Janārdana with dance, song, and instruments. / Having performed human worship to the god of gods, the wielder of the discus,
they had reached the presence of that very Parameṣṭhin. / Thousands of millions were seen; and having seen them, the night-roamer,

1.184.m:
with his hair standing on end, then departed from that place to another place. / He went and saw right there a house of incomparable qualities.
And he saw then a person lying upon a couch there; / with a pale, very precious cloth for his couch and seat,
that tiger among men was lying down, enveloped in fire, / his limbs smeared with divine perfumes, adorned with divine ornaments.
A virtuous woman wearing divine garments, the sole ornament of the three worlds, / holding a fly-whisk in her hand, peerless in beauty on earth,
placed the feet of that discus-wielding god upon her lap. / Wishing to seize that virtuous woman suddenly, [Rāvaṇa] fell forcibly before the rākṣasas.
Only the veil of that great soul was seen by him; / then the god laughed loudly on seeing that lord of rākṣasas.
By the splendour of that divine one, Rāvaṇa, who makes the world cry out, / fell to the surface of the earth like a tree cut down at the root.
To that fallen lord of rākṣasas, the god spoke these words: / “Rise! There is no death for you at present, O night-roamer.

तमब्रवीत्तदा राजा राक्षसानां तु विह्वलः ॥ 31 ॥
को भवाच्छयने शेते युगान्तानलसन्निभः ॥
एवमुक्तः स तेनाथ प्रत्युवाच निशाचरम् ॥ 32 ॥
कि ते मया दशग्रीव वध्योसि न चिरान्मम ॥
एवमेव च मृत्युस्ते भविष्यति दशानन ॥ 33 ॥
यां जिघृक्षसि मोहात्त्वं भूयश्चैनां हरिष्यसि ॥
मानुष्यमहमासाद्य त्वां वधिष्यामि रावण ॥ 34 ॥
अस्याः कृते विशालाक्ष्याः साम्प्रतं गच्छ राक्षस ॥
श्रुत्वैतद्वचनं देवाद्रावणो वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥ 35 ॥
नास्ति धन्यतरो लोके मया लोकत्रये विना ॥
त्वद्धस्तान्मरणं यस्य भविष्यति जगत्प्रभो ॥ ॥ 36 ॥
यशस्यं श्लाघनीयं च त्वद्धस्तान्मरणं मम ॥
अथास्य गात्रे संपश्यद्रावणो भीमविक्रमः ॥ 37 ॥
1.184.m:
It is by the boon of the Lord of Creatures, O rākṣasa, that you live at present.” / Then the king of the rākṣasas, bewildered, said to him:
“Who are you who lie upon the couch, resembling the fire at the end of the age?” / Addressed thus by him, he then replied to the night-roamer:
“What [concern] have you with me, O ten-necked one? You are to be slain by me before long; / and in this very manner your death will occur, O ten-faced one.
She whom you wish to seize out of delusion, you shall abduct her again; / having attained human form, I will slay you, O Rāvaṇa.
For the sake of this large-eyed lady [I spare you]; depart now, O rākṣasa.” / Hearing these words from the god, Rāvaṇa said:
“There is none more fortunate in the world, in all the three worlds, than me, / whose death will come from your hand, O Lord of the Universe!
Fame-bringing and praiseworthy is my death at your hands.” / Then, Rāvaṇa of terrifying valour looked upon his body.

1.239.7 Gifts of gold, and between the liver and the lungs.
His heart indeed is the puroḍāśa for Indra; the liver is for Savitṛ; the lungs are for Varuṇa. [Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa] 12.9.1.3.
1.240
Śailūṣa said:
I wish to hear accurately the slaying of Lavaṇa, O brahmin: / how Lavaṇa was struck down in battle by Śatrughna.
Nāḍāyana said:
While the son of Daśaratha was residing in unconquered Ayodhyā, O king, / on a certain occasion, when spring, which heightens delight, had not yet passed,
neither too hot nor too cold, comfortable and delighting all living beings, / when bees were humming sweetly, perched on blooming trees,
filled with the calling of cuckoos, the trees bearing fresh shoots, / at a time when the sun's rays were pleasant and the surface of the earth was adorned,
resounding with cuckoos perched on the topmost branches of leafy mangoes, / travelers wishing to depart on journeys were repeatedly turned back;

मञ्जर्यः सहकाराणां यत्र लग्ना शिलीमुखाः ॥
कामनामाङ्किता बाणाः कामस्येव शरीरिणाम् ॥ 6 ॥
कामिन्यः कामिनां कामं यत्र त्यजयतो दृढम् ॥
समीरणेन दाक्षिण्यं सर्वत्र प्रकटीकृतम् ॥ 7 ॥
मृदुप्रवातसंनुन्नप्रसूनयवशालिनी ॥
क्ष्वेडपङ्क्तिः सुरुरुचे वहमानेव निम्नगा ॥ 8 ॥
आलिङ्गितास्तु मधुना समन्ताद्वनराजयः ॥
फुल्लैः पलाशैः प्रकटं रागं बभ्रुस्तदा स्वयम् ॥ 9 ॥
समीरणेन मृदुना पुष्पपत्रार्चिता मही ॥
रात्रौ व्यभ्रस्य नभसः श्रियमूहे सशाद्वला ॥ 1.240.10 ॥
वञ्चितैर्नवजातानां वत्सानां मृदुभाषिणाम् ॥
गोष्ठेषु शोभा महती यस्मिन्गंधर्वसत्तम ॥ 11 ॥
हम्भारवविराविण्यः स्त्वरमाणपदक्रमाः ॥
यस्मिन्वत्सोत्सुका गावः प्रविशन्ति दिनक्षये ॥12॥
स्तनं पिबद्भिर्मातॄणां वत्सैरुत्क्षिप्तपुच्छकैः ॥
मुहुर्मुदं परां यत्र मातृलीढैस्तु गोपिनः ॥13॥

śrutvaiva nanṛturyatra mṛduvātahatā latāḥ ..15..
tasminvyatīte tu madhau narendra saṃtāpayāmāsa jagatsamagram ..
nidāghakālo lavaṇopamastu saṃruddhamārgo'tibṛhatpalāśaḥ .. 16 ..
1.184.d:
यत्र पुष्पोच्चयं चक्रुः कामिनीपाणिपल्लवाः ॥
पल्लवानां तु सादृश्याद्विज्ञाता नैव कामिभिः ॥14॥
ऋतुकोकिलसंगीतौ द्विरेफध्वनिवल्लकीम् ॥
श्रुत्वैव ननृतुर्यत्र मृदुवातहता लताः ॥15॥
तस्मिन्व्यतीते तु मधौ नरेन्द्र संतापयामास जगत्समग्रम् ॥
निदाघकालो लवणोपमस्तु संरुद्धमार्गोऽतिबृहत्पलाशः ॥ 16 ॥

.. nāḍāyana uvāca ..
vartamāne tadā grīṣme vikasanmallikākule ..
nivṛttapānthasaṃcāre saṃtaptasikatotkare..1..
